body:
This pull request introduces several important updates across documentation, security rules, and the mobile iOS app. The main highlights are the addition of detailed Firestore and Storage security rules, comprehensive UML diagrams documenting system and component architecture, and user experience improvements in the iOS app, including a new navigation link to the Terms of Use. Additionally, minor configuration and code cleanups are included.

**Security and Access Control**

* Added a comprehensive Firestore security rules file (`firestore.rules`) with granular access control for users, admins, conversations, messages, AI profiles, evaluations, settings, logs, and courses. This includes custom functions for role checks and field-level update restrictions.
* Added Firebase Storage security rules (`storage.rules`) enforcing that only admins can write, while signed-in users can read files. Public read access is allowed for AI avatars.

**Architecture Documentation**

* Added a suite of PlantUML diagrams and a README to the `docs/uml` directory, covering system context, Next.js and iOS component architecture, message flow, and RGPD account deletion flow. These diagrams provide a clear overview of the system's structure and key interactions. body:
## Summary
Refactored the inquiry dialog state management from React component state to a centralized Zustand store, eliminating prop drilling across the application. Added comprehensive unit tests for utility functions and core libraries.

## Key Changes

### State Management Refactoring
- Created `src/store/ui-store.ts` using Zustand to manage inquiry dialog state globally
- Removed `inquiryDialogOpen` state and `onOpenInquiry` prop from App component
- Updated all page components to use `useUIStore()` hook instead of receiving `onOpenInquiry` as a prop
- Removed prop interfaces from 20+ page components (HomePage, BranchenPage, LeistungenPage variants, etc.)
- Updated Header, GuaranteeBanner, ProcessTimeline, and StandCalculator components to use the store

### Error Handling
- Added `PageErrorBoundary` component using react-error-boundary for graceful error handling
- Integrated error boundary in App component to wrap page renders

### Testing Infrastructure
- Added Vitest configuration and test setup
- Created unit tests for:
  - `rate-limiter.ts` - Rate limiting logic with cooldown and request tracking
  - `i18n.ts` - Translation and language storage functionality
  - `deep-linking.ts` - Page path normalization and header offset constants
  - `utils.ts` - className merging utility (cn function)
- Added npm scripts: `test` and `test:watch`

### Code Organization
- Split demo data into separate files:
  - `demo-references.ts` (extracted from demo-data.ts)
  - `demo-blog-posts.ts` (extracted from demo-data.ts)
- Updated all imports across components to use new demo data modules

### Configuration
- Added `.env.example` with VITE_API_BASE configuration
- Updated `api-client.ts` to use environment variable for API base URL
- Added Zustand dependency to package.json

### Code Quality
- Fixed whitespace inconsistencies throughout App.tsx
- Improved component prop interfaces by removing unnecessary prop drilling

## Implementation Details
The Zustand store provides a simple, performant alternative to prop drilling with methods like `openInquiry()` and `setInquiryOpen()` accessible throughout the application. The error boundary ensures failed page loads display user-friendly error messages instead of blank screens. Test coverage focuses on critical utility functions and library functionality to catch regressions early.

author: claude
body:
The language support tester workflow was failing with "method is invalid during session initialization" errors because the Serena MCP server container was being pulled on-demand during gateway startup, causing initialization timeouts.

## Changes

- **Added container pre-pull step** in workflow frontmatter to download `ghcr.io/github/serena-mcp-server:latest` during setup phase, before MCP gateway initialization

```yaml
steps:
  - name: Set up Go
    uses: actions/setup-go@4dc6199c7b1a012772edbd06daecab0f50c9053c # v6
    with:
      go-version-file: go.mod
      cache: true
  - name: Pull Serena MCP Server Container
    run: docker pull ghcr.io/github/serena-mcp-server:latest
```

By caching the container image before the gateway starts, the Serena backend launches immediately when needed, eliminating the download latency that caused initialization to appear incomplete.

## Note

The `.lock.yml` file will need recompilation via `gh aw compile` or will be automatically updated during merge.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>[language-support] Serena MCP Server fails to complete initialization - All language support tests failing</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Problem Summary
> 
> All language support tests (Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, and Python) are failing because the Serena MCP server backend never completes its initialization sequence.
> 
> ## Error Details
> 
> After successfully calling `initialize` and sending the `notifications/initialized` message, any subsequent MCP method call (including `tools/list` and `tools/call`) returns:
> 
> ````json
> {
>   "code": 0,
>   "message": "method \"tools/call\" is invalid during session initialization"
> }
> ````
> 
> This error persists even after waiting 10+ seconds for the backend to initialize.
> 
> ## Reproduction Steps
> 
> 1. Initialize a session with Serena MCP server:
> ````bash
> curl -X POST (host.docker.internal/redacted) \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -H "Authorization: (token)" \
>   -d '{
>     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
>     "id": 1,
>     "method": "initialize",
>     "params": {
>       "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
>       "capabilities": {},
>       "clientInfo": {"name": "test", "version": "1.0"}
>     }
>   }'
> ````
> 
> 2. Send initialized notification:
> ````bash
> curl -X POST (host.docker.internal/redacted) \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -H "Authorization: (token)" \
>   -d '{
>     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
>     "method": "notifications/initialized",
>     "params": {}
>   }'
> ````
> 
> 3. Wait (even 10+ seconds)
> 
> 4. Try any method (tools/list, tools/call, etc.) - all fail with "invalid during session initialization"
> 
> ## Expected Behavior
> 
> After sending `notifications/initialized`, the backend MCP server should complete its initialization and allow method calls like `tools/list`, `tools/call`, etc.
> 
> ## Actual Behavior
> 
> The session remains stuck in "initialization" state indefinitely. No MCP methods can be called.
> 
> ## Impact
> 
> - **Go language support**: ❌ FAIL
> - **TypeScript/JavaScript language support**: ❌ FAIL  
> - **Python language support**: ❌ FAIL
> 
> All language analysis features are completely non-functional.
> 
> ## Environment
> 
> - Workflow: `language-support-tester`
> - MCP Gateway: `ghcr.io/github/gh-aw-mcpg` (Docker-in-Docker configuration)
> - Serena MCP Server: `ghcr.io/github/serena-mcp-server:latest`
> - Test projects: `/test/serena-mcp-tests/samples/{go,js,python}_project`
> 
> ## Possible Root Causes
> 
> 1. **Gateway issue**: The MCP gateway may not be properly relaying the `notifications/initialized` message to the Serena backend
> 2. **Backend issue**: The Serena MCP server may not be handling the initialization notification correctly
> 3. **Session state issue**: The gateway may be checking session state before the backend has confirmed readiness
> 
> ## Suggested Investigation
> 
> 1. Check MCP gateway logs for Serena backend communication
> 2. Verify that `notifications/initialized` is being forwarded to the Serena container
> 3. Check if Serena backend sends any response/acknowledgment after receiving the notification
> 4. Review session state management in the gateway's initialization flow
> 
> ## Testing Notes
> 
> - Session initialization succeeds (returns proper capabilities)
> - Response includes valid session ID in headers
> - SSE format responses are properly formatted
> - Authorization works correctly
> - Only post-initialization method calls fail
>

body:
Fix to resolve generate and post PR.


> Root cause: The "Test" step has continue-on-error: true, which prevents the job from entering a "failed" state when tests fail. GitHub's failure() status function only returns true if the job is actually in a failed state — so both the "Generate PR Comment" and "Post PR Comment" steps were silently skipped.

author: pcortez
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complete PDF text extraction library written in pure Go with no external dependencies. It is a port of [zpdf](https://github.com/Lulzx/zpdf) and provides comprehensive PDF parsing and text extraction capabilities.

## Key Changes

- **PDF Document Parsing** (`document.go`): Implements core PDF document loading with support for:
  - XRef table and cross-reference stream (PDF 1.5+) parsing
  - Indirect object resolution with caching
  - Compressed object streams
  - Trailer dictionary handling
  - Support for incremental updates via `Prev` chains

- **Content Stream Parser** (`parser.go`): Recursive-descent parser for PDF objects supporting:
  - All PDF object types (null, bool, int, float, string, name, array, dict, stream, reference)
  - Hex string and literal string parsing with escape sequences
  - Dictionary and array parsing with nesting depth limits
  - Name escape sequence decoding

- **Text Extraction** (`extractor.go`): Extracts plain text from PDF pages by:
  - Parsing content stream operators (Tj, TJ, Td, Tm, BT, ET, etc.)
  - Tracking text positioning and transformation matrices
  - Handling text arrays with kerning values
  - Sorting text spans by position for logical reading order
  - Filtering control characters and normalizing whitespace

- **Font Encoding** (`encoding.go`): Decodes glyph codes to Unicode with:
  - Support for simple fonts (single-byte) and CID fonts (multi-byte)
  - ToUnicode CMap parsing (highest priority)
  - Standard PDF encodings (WinAnsi, MacRoman, StandardEncoding, PDFDocEncoding)
  - Encoding dictionary with /Differences array support
  - UTF-16BE to UTF-8 conversion

- **Stream Decompression** (`decompress.go`): Handles multiple PDF filters:
  - FlateDecode with PNG/TIFF predictor support
  - ASCII85Decode and ASCIIHexDecode
  - LZWDecode and RunLengthDecode
  - Filter chains (multiple filters applied sequentially)
  - DoS protection via 256 MB decompression limit

- **Comprehensive Tests** (`extractor_test.go`): Test suite covering:
  - Simple text extraction
  - TJ operator with kerning
  - Multi-page documents
  - Page info retrieval
  - Stream decompression filters

- **Documentation**: Updated README with usage examples and API reference

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Zero Dependencies**: Uses only Go standard library (compress/zlib, compress/lzw, encoding/ascii85)
- **Memory Safety**: Bounds checking on all byte operations, decompression size limits
- **PDF 1.5+ Support**: Handles modern PDF features including compressed object streams and cross-reference streams
- **Robust Parsing**: Graceful error handling with fallbacks for malformed PDFs
- **Text Positioning**: Maintains text state machine for accurate position tracking during extraction
- **CMap Support**: Full ToUnicode CMap parsing including bf-char and bf-range entries with array forms

author: rdzman
body:
It turns out the MATLAB Compiler does not support out-of-process calls to MEX files, only in-process.

With this PR, `callhighs()` uses `is_deployed()` to decide whether to use in-process or out-of-process call to `highsmex()`, allowing HiGHSMEX to be included in a compiled MATLAB program.

Also, it is now trivial to use an in-process MEX call in desktop MATLAB by uncommenting the `useMexHostByDefault = false` line.

FWIW, in my testing the out-of-process call can add some non-trivial overhead. With some code I have that calls HiGHS repeatedly to solve lots of LP and MILP problems, I observed runtime improvements on the order of 7-30% just by switching to in-process.

I'm curious what your reasons were for choosing to use the out-of-process approach?

Actually, it might be nice to have both approaches available. What do you think of including something like a separate `callhighs_in_process()` wrapper that always uses the in-process MEX call.

body:
## Summary

- CASE expressions on symbol columns with static symbol tables now resolve
  string constants to integer symbol keys at `init()` time and compare by
  int at runtime, avoiding per-row string comparisons.
- Three picker specializations based on branch count: single-branch (one `==`),
  dual-branch (two `==` comparisons), and multi-branch (`IntObjHashMap` lookup).

I recommend reviewing per-commit.

Adds back the `streaming_brief` feature, which really only is noticeable in a niche circumstance where `streaming_brief=True` and a logging event with a verbosity level `> logging.DEBUG` is received. Below is a minimal script to demonstrate this behavior.

```py
import logging
import subprocess
from time import sleep

from craft_cli import EmitterMode
from craft_cli._rs.emitter import Emitter

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

e = Emitter("blah.log", EmitterMode.BRIEF, "example.com", "Hello", streaming_brief=True)
logger.info("Testing")
with e.open_stream("Counting") as pipe:
    for i in range(5):
        logger.info("Printing %d", i)
        sleep(0.3)
        subprocess.run(["echo", str(i)], check=True, stdout=pipe)
        sleep(0.3)

e.message("Done")
```

As a fly-by, this adds back the ability to prefix messages piped with `Emitter.open_stream`, as mentioned at https://github.com/canonical/craft-cli/pull/416#discussion_r2800282094. This behavior is shown in the testing script as well.

author: marksant
body:
# Phase 4.3 — Decompose Detector God Class

## Summary

Decomposes the monolithic `Detector` class (2,607 lines, ~55 methods) into **5 focused modules**, each with a single responsibility and under 1,100 lines.

## New Modules

| Module | Lines | Responsibility |
|--------|-------|---------------|
| `detection_types.py` | ~120 | `ZoneData`, `AquariumData`, `MultiAquariumZoneData` data classes |
| `zone_scaler.py` | ~360 | Polygon scaling, point-in-polygon tests, crop helpers, scaling cache |
| `detection_post_processor.py` | ~480 | Stateless detection validation, tracking config, ByteTrack helpers |
| `single_detector.py` | ~1,035 | Single-aquarium detection, tracking (ByteTrack + SingleSubjectTracker), overlay |
| `multi_aquarium_detector.py` | ~1,070 | Multi-aquarium partitioned/parallel detection with independent trackers |

## Architecture

- **Composition pattern**: Shared `ZoneScaler` + `DetectionPostProcessor` injected into both `SingleDetector` and `MultiAquariumDetector`
- **Backward-compatible** via gutted `detector.py` re-export shim: `Detector = SingleDetector` alias
- All 94 existing import sites continue to work without changes

## Key Changes

### Source
- `detector.py` → Re-export shim only (~50 lines)
- `processing_worker.py` → Creates `MultiAquariumDetector` alongside `SingleDetector` when multi-aquarium zones detected
- `live_camera_service.py` → Lazily creates `MultiAquariumDetector` in `_run_multi_aquarium_detection`
- `detector_service.py` → Wires `ZoneScaler` + `DetectionPostProcessor` into constructor

### Tests Updated
- `test_detector.py` — Patch targets updated for moved internal methods
- `test_detector_partitioned.py` — Uses `MultiAquariumDetector` fixture
- `test_processing_worker_unit.py` — `FakeDetector` accepts new kwargs
- `test_parallel_detection_benchmark.py` — Uses correct detector types

## Validation

- **2,400 fast tests passing**, 0 regressions
- **Ruff lint**: All checks passed
- **Pre-commit**: All hooks passed

## Metrics

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `detector.py` lines | 2,607 | ~50 (re-export shim) |
| Largest new module | — | 1,070 (multi_aquarium_detector) |
| Backward-compat breaks | — | 0 |
| Test failures | — | 0 |

author: kwbr
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where percentage signs in width/height arguments (e.g., `-w75%` `-h90%`) were being stripped during argument processing.

## Root Cause

Arguments are expanded through tmux's `display-message` to support format string interpolation (e.g., `#{pane_current_path}`). The `%` character followed by a newline in format strings is interpreted as a format directive by tmux and gets stripped.

## Minimal Reproducible Test

```bash
tmux display-message -p "$(printf '75%%\n@@@@@\n')"  # Returns: 75% ✓
tmux display-message -p "$(printf '75%%\nmore\n')"   # Returns: 75  ✗ (stripped!)
```

## Why Existing Tests Didn't Catch This

The test suite uses a mock tmux command (`src/toggle_tests/tmux`) that intercepts calls to `batch_get_options` and returns values via `fake_batch_options`. This fake implementation outputs values verbatim without processing them through real `tmux display-message`, so it never encounters the `%` stripping behavior.

The tests validate argument parsing logic but not the actual tmux format expansion behavior. This is a test coverage gap where mocking prevented detection of a real integration issue.

## Changes

**src/toggle.sh**: Escape `%` as `%%` before expansion. Tmux automatically converts `%%` back to `%` during format string processing, so the values are correctly preserved.

## Test Plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (though they use mocked tmux)
- [x] Verified with real tmux that the command `toggle.sh -w75% -h90% --name=test` now generates `display-popup -w 75% -h 90%` with percentage signs preserved
- [x] Existing test `open_with_style` covers the code path with percentage values in width/height

author: clovenbradshaw-ctrl
body:
## Summary
Substantially revised the habeas corpus petition template to reflect current immigration detention law and recent legal developments, particularly the Board of Immigration Appeals' September 2025 ruling in Matter of Yajure Hurtado and subsequent federal court decisions.

## Key Changes

- **Introduction section**: Expanded from a single paragraph to a comprehensive 5-paragraph introduction that establishes the factual background, explains the BIA's recent precedential ruling, and articulates the core legal argument regarding statutory interpretation of §1226(a) vs §1225(b)(2).

- **Custody section**: Simplified and clarified language to establish jurisdiction under habeas corpus statute with proper case citation (Jones v. Cunningham).

- **Jurisdiction section**: Enhanced with explicit citations to multiple jurisdictional bases including 28 U.S.C. §2241, §1331, the Suspension Clause, and the INA, plus supporting case law (Zadvydas v. Davis).

- **Requirements section**: Reframed to address statutory procedural requirements under 28 U.S.C. §2243 regarding show cause orders and return deadlines.

- **Exhaustion section**: Renamed and substantially expanded to explain why administrative exhaustion is futile under the new BIA interpretation, with citations to recent district court decisions recognizing this futility.

- **Parties section**: Restructured to clearly delineate each respondent's role and custodial authority, distinguishing between immediate custodian, legal custodian, and ultimate legal custodian.

- **Legal Background section**: Renamed to "Legal Background and Argument" and dramatically expanded from 2 paragraphs to 15 paragraphs providing comprehensive statutory analysis, regulatory history, Supreme Court precedent, and citations to 9 recent federal court decisions supporting Petitioner's position.

- **Statement of Facts**: Reorganized and expanded to provide clearer factual narrative with specific paragraph numbering.

- **Count I**: Refocused on violation of §1226(a) with clearer articulation of entitlement to bond hearing.

- **Count II**: Updated to reference specific regulatory provisions (8 C.F.R. §§236.1, 1236.1, 1003.19) and the 1997 interim rule establishing the regulatory framework.

- **Count III**: Enhanced Due Process analysis with explicit application of Mathews v. Eldridge balancing test and additional supporting case law.

- **Prayer for Relief**: Expanded from 6 to 8 requests with more specific relief sought, including expedited consideration, non-transfer order, and explicit reference to Equal Access to Justice Act.

- **Verification**: Updated signature block to accommodate multiple attorneys and revised language to reflect counsel verification on behalf of petitioner.

## Notable Implementation Details

The revision reflects a shift from a generic habeas petition template to one specifically tailored to address the legal landscape following the BIA's September 2025 Yajure Hurtado ruling, incorporating recent federal court precedent and emphasizing statutory interpretation arguments under the Loper Light framework.

author: morde08
body:
## Summary
- Adds a `scope` column (indexed, not encrypted) to `memory_vault` for partitioning memories by visibility (e.g., `"private"` for Anuma, `"public"` for GPT/Gemini)
- Defaults to `"private"` scope on create; migration backfills existing rows
- Scope is filterable and mutable via vault operations

## Integration
- `createVaultMemory({ content, scope? })` — pass scope when creating memories
- `getVaultMemories({ scopes: [...] })` — filter by scope
- `createMemoryVaultTool({ scope })` — set scope for LLM-created memories
- `createMemoryVaultSearchTool({ scopes: [...] })` — restrict search to specific scopes
- `updateVaultMemory(id, { content, scope? })` — change a memory's scope

## Breaking Changes
- `StoredVaultMemory` now has a required `scope: string` field
- Schema version bumped from 14 to 15 (automatic migration adds `scope` column, backfills to `"private"`)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Includes a persistent schema migration and makes `scope` required on `StoredVaultMemory`, which can break downstream callers and affect memory retrieval results if not migrated/queried correctly.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a required `scope` field to memory vault records to support partitioning (e.g. private vs public), including a schema/migration bump to v16 that backfills existing rows to `private`.
> 
> Vault CRUD/search APIs are extended to set a default `private` scope on create, optionally update scope, and filter `getAllVaultMemoriesOp`/`getVaultMemories`/pre-embed/search by allowed scopes; React/Expo `useChatStorage` surface area is updated accordingly. Test coverage is added/updated across vault operations and tools to validate scope defaults, filtering behavior, and that scope is not encrypted or LLM-controlled except via client configuration.
>

💡 **What:** Implemented a debounce mechanism (300ms) for the `fetchEvents` call triggered by `visibilitychange` and `focus` events in `frontend/app/events/page.tsx`.
🎯 **Why:** To prevent redundant API calls when a user switches tabs or refocuses the window, as both events often fire in rapid succession, causing unnecessary load on the server.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Verified via a simulation script that the number of fetch calls is reduced from 2 to 1 when both events fire within a short interval. This eliminates duplicate requests on every tab switch.

With this change, provider-specific behaviour is declared once in `resolveProviderCapabilities()` and all consumers query the capability they need — no provider string comparisons at call sites. ## Test plan - [ ] Verify Anthropic provider: prompt cache, transcript sanitization, turn validation unchanged - [ ] Verify Google provider: tool schema stripping, turn ordering fix unchanged - [ ] Verify Mistral provider: strict-9 tool call ID mode unchanged - [ ] Verify OpenRouter: attribution headers injected, Gemini thought-signature sanitization unchanged - [ ] Verify OpenAI provider: apply_patch tool gated correctly, images-only sanitize mode - [ ] Verify ZAI: `supportsDeveloperRole: false` still applied via `normalizeModelCompat` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: midlan
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces DomBuilder, a system for compressing HTML into a compact instruction format, compressing it with deflate, and encoding it as base64url for use in URL hashes. It includes both a decoder for rendering compressed HTML and an editor for creating and sharing compressed HTML URLs.

## Key Changes

- **New `dombuilder.js` module**: Core library providing:
  - Instruction executor: Interprets a simple instruction set (E/A/T/^) to build DOM elements
  - HTML-to-instructions converter: Parses HTML and generates the instruction format
  - Compression/decompression: Uses CompressionStream API with deflate-raw
  - Base64url encoding/decoding: Converts compressed bytes to URL-safe strings
  - High-level encode/decode functions for end-to-end workflows

- **Simplified `index.html`**: Replaced complex URL parameter parsing with:
  - Single hash-based decoder that reads compressed instructions from the URL fragment
  - Calls `decodeInstructions()` and `executeInstructions()` to render the DOM
  - Error handling for decode failures

- **New `editor.html`**: Interactive editor for creating shareable URLs:
  - Split-pane UI with HTML source editor and live preview
  - "Run" button converts HTML → instructions → compressed URL
  - Displays the resulting shareable URL in a copy-friendly input field
  - Preview renders via the instruction executor for validation

## Implementation Details

- Instructions use a line-based format: `E tag`, `A name value`, `T text`, `^` (pop)
- Text escaping: `\\` for backslash, `\n` for newline
- Compression via native CompressionStream API (deflate-raw format)
- Base64url encoding removes padding and uses URL-safe characters
- Both encoder and decoder are async to support streaming compression APIs

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CAZxB9pJJmC3nph4AjqG4s

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it replaces the URL parsing/rendering mechanism and adds a custom compression/encoding pipeline plus new deployment automation, which could break existing links or Pages publishing if assumptions are wrong.
> 
> **Overview**
> Switches the app from query-style hash parsing to a **compressed instruction format** stored in the URL hash, with `index.html` now decoding and executing instructions to rebuild the DOM at runtime.
> 
> Adds a new `dombuilder.js` core module (instruction executor, HTML→instruction conversion, deflate-raw compression, base64url encode/decode) and an `editor.html` split-panel editor that generates shareable URLs and previews output.
> 
> Updates GitHub Actions to **deploy on tags** into per-tag directories on `gh-pages`, maintain a `/latest/` symlink, and generate a root release index; adds a Node 20 CI workflow that roundtrips encode/decode against example HTML fixtures. Updates `README.md` to document the new editor, encoding approach, and versioned deployments.

author: anveio
body:
## Summary

- Add new `apm2_core::fac::queue_bounds` module implementing hard queue-level bounds on pending job count and total bytes with structured denial receipts (TCK-00578)
- Three enforcement dimensions: `max_pending_jobs` (default 10K), `max_pending_bytes` (default 10 GiB), and optional `per_lane_max_pending_jobs`
- Integrate bounds checking into CLI `enqueue_job()` path -- bounds are evaluated BEFORE writing job specs to disk (INV-QB-002), fail-closed on scan errors or arithmetic overflow

## Key Design Decisions

- **Defense-in-depth**: Complements TCK-00568 per-window rate limits with absolute queue size bounds
- **Bounded I/O**: `scan_pending_queue` caps directory iteration at `MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES=100,000` entries and lane tracking at `MAX_TRACKED_LANES=256` (CTR-1303)
- **Symlink-safe**: All file metadata reads use `symlink_metadata` (no symlink following, CTR-1503)
- **Fail-closed**: Zero limits deny all enqueues; scan failures deny fail-closed; counter overflow denied via `checked_add`
- **Structured denial receipts**: `QueueQuotaDenialReceipt` carries dimension, current usage, limit, proposed increment, stable reason code, and optional lane for audit

## Security Invariants

- [INV-QB-001] Fail-closed: scan failure or overflow denies the enqueue
- [INV-QB-002] Bounds check occurs BEFORE the job spec is written to disk
- [INV-QB-003] Denial receipts include exceeded dimension, current usage, limit, and stable reason code
- [INV-QB-004] All string fields in receipts are bounded (`MAX_DENIAL_REASON_LENGTH=256`)
- [INV-QB-005] Directory scan bounded by `MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES` to prevent DoS
- [INV-QB-006] File metadata reads use `symlink_metadata` per CTR-1503

## Test Plan

- [x] 29 unit tests covering all dimensions, overflow, flooding, serialization round-trips, UTF-8 safety
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes clean

author: coreyb-git
body:
When signcolumn has an "auto" setting this causes a UI redraw event that resizes the gutter inwards due to there being less icons in the gutter.  Next, repopulating the diagnostics causes another UI redraw to resize the gutter back outwards to account for the re-adding of all the spellwarn diagnostics.  This is a rapid visual glitch.

Diagnostics doesn't require a reset for NeoVim to automatically remove the entries that are no longer in the newly set diagnostics list of a namespace (at least in NeoVim v12), thus the reset function is unnecessary, and only serves to create visual glitching with every spelling mistake fixed or created when the signcolumn width is "auto".

author: stellaraccident
body:
## Summary

Three fixes that together enable rocRAND (and other multi-TU libraries) to work correctly with kpack split artifacts:

- **PHDR alignment fix**: `conservative_zero_page()` did not adjust `e_phoff` after removing bytes, and `get_min_content_offset()` included PT_LOAD at offset 0, causing alignment violations that made `ld.so` reject transformed binaries. Adds 9 tests in `test_zero_page.py`.

- **Runtime .kpm manifest resolution**: The loader now detects `.kpm` manifest files in search paths, parses them, and opens the corresponding `.kpack` archives. Also strips `amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--` prefix from architecture names for archive lookup.

- **Multi-TU concatenated bundle extraction**: Libraries built with `-fgpu-rdc` have multiple `__CLANG_OFFLOAD_BUNDLE__` blocks concatenated in `.hip_fatbin`. `clang-offload-bundler` only sees the first one. Added `ccob_parser` support to detect and extract all bundles, with dispatch in `binutils.py`.

## Test plan

- [x] All 377 rocm-kpack unit tests pass
- [x] All 46 rocRAND test suites pass (previously 20+ were failing with TOC key mismatches)
- [x] Pre-commit passes on all changed files

## Summary

- **globals.css**: Replaced colour palette with warm amber/cream (light) and deep slate-purple (dark) CSS custom properties. Added `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query targeting `:root:not(.light)` so the class-based toggle always wins over system preference. Added smooth `transition` on `body` for theme switching.
- **Header.tsx**: Added dark mode toggle button (moon/sun SVG icons) that reads the initial state from `localStorage` with a system-preference fallback. Persists the user choice to `localStorage` under key `mochi-theme` and updates the `.dark` / `.light` class on `<html>` on every toggle. A `MediaQueryList` listener keeps the toggle in sync when the OS setting changes and no explicit preference is stored.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open app in a light-system browser — should render warm cream/amber
- [ ] Open app in a dark-system browser — should render slate-purple background without clicking anything
- [ ] Click the moon button → dark mode activates, icon changes to sun
- [ ] Reload page → dark mode persists (localStorage)
- [ ] Click sun button → light mode restores, persists on reload
- [ ] Clear localStorage, change OS to dark → app follows system preference
- [ ] After setting explicit preference, changing OS preference should NOT change app theme

Closes #4 (parent: #3)

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>crossplane/crossplane (crossplane/crossplane)</summary>

### [`v2.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/releases/tag/v2.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/compare/v2.1.4...v2.2.0)

The `v2.2.0` release is a regular quarterly Crossplane release that is focused on maturing a number of key areas of functionality across the project, as Crossplane continues to become more capable, more reliable, and more performant for your production workloads. This release includes many fixes and reliability improvements, a new alpha feature for debugging (the pipeline inspector), and usability improvements.

#### ℹ️ Extended support for `v1.20`

Normally, the release of `v2.2` would correspond with the end-of-life for `v1.20`. However, because `v1.20` is the last minor release of the `v1` series and major version upgrades require additional planning for users, `v1.20` will continue to receive critical fixes. The final EOL date for `v1.20` is to be determined.

#### ⚠️ Upgrade from `v2.1`

It is strongly advised to upgrade to `v2.2` from the previous minor version, which is `v2.1`.  Upon upgrade for each minor release, Crossplane performs any necessary migrations of its CRDs to ensure the latest versions are stored in the Kubernetes API server. Therefore, it is important to upgrade sequentially through one minor version at a time as described in the [upgrade docs](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/upgrade-crossplane/).

#### 🚨 Notable and Breaking Changes

- Input CRDs included in `Function` packages are no longer installed by the package manager, following the xpkg specification. Unknown or disallowed resources in a package are now ignored instead of causing package installation to fail. See [#​6976](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/6976).
- The on-disk structure of the package cache has changed. This breaks an undocumented behavior via which packages could be side-loaded into Crossplane, which was especially useful for testing. See [#​6981](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/6981) for details on the change and [#​7147](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7147) for discussion of the test changes necessary to accommodate it.

#### 🎉 Highlights

- `ImageConfig` can now be used to configure the `DeploymentRuntimeConfig` used for packages, including those installed as dependencies. Note that a matching `ImageConfig` takes precedence over the `runtimeConfigRef` in a package spec if both are present. See [#​6382](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/6382).
- The MRD controller now uses server-side apply to update CRDs, improving reliability. See [#​6934](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/6934).
- The pipeline inspector is now available as an alpha feature (disabled by default). When enabled, the inspector forwards function requests and responses to a user-configured gRPC endpoint for debugging or observability. See [#​7025](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7025) and [#​7031](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7031).
- XRDs can now configure `x-kubernetes-validations` outside of the spec. This allows for validation of metadata such as names and labels. See [#​7018](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7018).
- Composition and operation functions can now request OpenAPI schemas for any resource kind in the cluster using the `RequiredSchemas` field in the function response. Crossplane now advertises capabilities (including required schemas) to functions in a new function request field. See [#​7022](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7022).
- The `crossplane beta trace` CLI command now supports tracing all resources of a given kind, and supports watching resources. See [#​6552](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/6552) and [#​7015](https://redirect.github.com/crossplane/crossplane/issues/7015).
- New documentation has been added regarding [connection details for composite resources](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/connection-details-composition/) and [workload identity with Crossplane](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/crossplane-with-workload-identity/).

#### 🏅 Release MVP

[@​jonasz-lasut](https://redirect.github.com/jonasz-lasut) is the `v2.2` release MVP! Their work driving enhancements, fixing bugs, and maintaining quality across Crossplane and its ecosystem is much appreciated by the Crossplane maintainers. Additionally, [@​jonasz-lasut](https://redirect.github.com/jonasz-lasut) is an active participant on the Crossplane Slack instance, answering questions and providing guidance to many new and experienced members of the community. Thank you for your dedication, [@​jonasz-lasut](https://redirect.github.com/jonasz-lasut)! :tada:

author: smith
body:
## Summary

Closes #248341

Adds support for the `observability:enableInspectEsQueries` advanced setting in the Infrastructure Hosts UI. When the setting is enabled, an **Inspect** header link opens the inspector panel showing all Elasticsearch queries made by the page — including request params, response data, and timing stats. This follows the pattern established by APM and Synthetics.

### Backend

- **`withInspect` wrapper** (`server/lib/helpers/with_inspect.ts`): A reusable route handler wrapper that manages a per-request `WeakMap<KibanaRequest, InspectResponse>` to collect ES query metadata. When `_inspect=true` is in the query string, the collected data is appended to the response body. On error, it's attached as `attributes._inspect`. This replaces the manual try/catch + `response.ok()`/`response.customError()` pattern in each route — handlers now just return data or throw.
- **`getInfraMetricsClient` instrumentation**: `search()` and `msearch()` now accept an optional `operationName` and record request/response metadata via `getInspectResponse()` from `@kbn/observability-shared-plugin` when a collector is present for the request.
- **Route opt-in**: Added `_inspect` query param validation (`jsonRt.pipe(rt.boolean)`) to the hosts, count, snapshot, and metadata routes. Each route handler is wrapped with `withInspect`.

### Frontend

- **`inspector` plugin dependency** added to `kibana.jsonc` and `types.ts`.
- **`InspectorContextProvider`** wraps the metrics app routes.
- **`InspectorHeaderLink`** component: conditionally renders an "Inspect" link in the header when the setting is enabled.
- **`useFetcher` integration**: `createInfraApiClient` replaces `createAutoAbortedClient`. For inspectable routes (allowlisted by path), it appends `_inspect=true` to the query and feeds responses to the inspector adapter via `addInspectorRequest`. Non-inspectable routes are unaffected.

### Testing

- Unit tests for `withInspect` covering: normal response, `_inspect=true` inclusion, `_inspect` absence, error with inspect data, and WeakMap cleanup.
- Existing `getInfraMetricsClient` tests updated for the new `operationName` parameter.

## Test plan

- [ ] Enable `observability:enableInspectEsQueries` in Stack Management > Advanced Settings
- [ ] Navigate to Infrastructure > Hosts
- [ ] Verify "Inspect" link appears in the header
- [ ] Click "Inspect" — panel should show ES queries with Statistics, Request, and Response tabs
- [ ] Verify each request has a descriptive operation name (e.g. "get all hosts", "get hosts count")
- [ ] Disable the setting and verify the "Inspect" link disappears
- [ ] Run `yarn test:jest x-pack/solutions/observability/plugins/infra/server/lib/helpers/with_inspect.test.ts`

author: gsinghjay
body:
## Summary

- Removes temporary `console.log` statements from `astro.config.mjs` that were used to debug Cloudflare Pages environment variable injection

## Background

While fixing GA4 analytics on production, we added debug logging to `astro.config.mjs` to see which environment variables were available during Cloudflare Pages builds. The logs helped us discover:

1. **CF Pages dashboard plaintext variables DO get injected into `process.env`** during builds
2. **The `@astrojs/cloudflare` adapter blocks Vite's normal env var handling** — it sets `define: { "process.env": "process.env" }` which prevents Vite from automatically making `PUBLIC_*` vars available via `import.meta.env` in `.astro` files
3. **The fix (already in this branch):** Read env vars in `astro.config.mjs` (where `process.env` works) and pass them through Vite's `define` config so they're available in `.astro` files during prerendering

## What this PR does

Removes the 6 `console.log` lines that were printing env var values to the build log. The actual fix (Vite `define` bridge) stays in place.

## What stays and why

The `astro.config.mjs` now has this pattern for any `PUBLIC_*` var that `.astro` files need:

```javascript
// 1. Read from process.env in astro.config.mjs (works on CF Pages)
const gaId = env.PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID || process.env.PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID || "";

// 2. Pass through Vite's define so .astro files can use import.meta.env
define: {
  "import.meta.env.PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID": JSON.stringify(gaId),
}
```

**If you add a new `PUBLIC_*` variable in the future** that needs to be read in `.astro` files, you'll need to:
1. Add it to the CF Pages dashboard (as Plaintext, NOT encrypted)
2. Add the `loadEnv`/`process.env` fallback line in `astro.config.mjs`
3. Add it to the `define` block in `astro.config.mjs`

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify production GA4 still works after merging (no regression from removing logs)
- [ ] Verify preview visual editing still works

author: hoxit1006-ops
body:
### Motivation
- Improve extraction reliability so messy OCR output still yields complete items and official totals (subtotal/tax/total) for each receipt. 
- Give users a higher-accuracy fallback by leveraging a ChatGPT-based extraction when rule-based OCR parsing misses lines or mis-parses prices.
- Surface merchant detection and make parsed data editable before saving to minimize manual corrections.

### Description
- UI: added an `OpenAI API key` input and an `AI parse from OCR text` button in `index.html` so users can optionally run ChatGPT extraction in-browser without persisting the key. 
- Local parsing: implemented `parseReceiptText`, `parseTotals`, `extractMerchant`, line cleanup, quantity detection, price token matching, and deduplication in `script.js` to better handle noisy OCR and pasted text. 
- AI integration: added `parseWithOpenAI` which calls the OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`, model `gpt-4.1-mini`) to request structured JSON `{merchant, subtotal, tax, total, items[...]}` and map results to the app data model with category guessing. 
- Storage/UI sync: parsed `subtotal`, `tax`, and `total` are stored alongside `items` and shown in the spending summary and receipt history, while keeping the editable item-rows and junk-food savings calculation intact. 

### Testing
- Ran `node --check script.js` which completed successfully. 
- Launched a local static server and validated serving with `python3 -m http.server 4173` and `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:4173` returning `200 OK`.

## Summary

- Allow `@expr` attributes to navigate through declared `between` relationships to access attributes on related entities (e.g. `DeptEmployee.Department.BudgetMultiplier`)
- Add compile-time validation that rejects invalid relationship references: many-to-many, one-to-many from the "one" side, wrong entity aliases, and references to the same side

- Resolve related instances at runtime via fast path (creation through relationship pattern) and slow path (query for updates)

author: copilot
body:
Chat-based concierge ("Eleanor") that parses natural language like *"order me a pizza, also book me a haircut for Monday at 10"*, identifies multiple intents, and executes tools to satisfy them — all with visible agent reasoning steps.

## Architecture

- **`app/page.tsx`** — Landing page + chat UI with thinking-steps accordion and per-tool receipt cards. Integrates patterns from existing `frontend/` components.
- **`app/api/agent/route.ts`** — POST endpoint: parses intents via `AgentBrain`, executes tools from registry, returns structured `AgentResponse`.
- **`lib/agent/mock-brain.ts`** — `MockBrain` implements `AgentBrain` using regex heuristics for pizza/haircut/booking keywords. Default simulation mode — no cloud credentials needed.
- **`lib/agent/tools.ts`** — Tool registry with `orderPizza` and `bookAppointment` executors.
- **`lib/agent/types.ts`** — `AgentBrain` interface for swapping in Vertex AI later, plus `ToolCall`, `ThinkingStep`, `ToolResult` types.
- **`Dockerfile`** + **`docker-compose.yml`** — Multi-stage standalone build; `docker-compose up` → `localhost:3000`.

## Example

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/agent \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Order me a pizza and book a haircut for Monday at 10"}'
```

Returns 2 tool calls with receipts, 6 thinking steps, and a combined summary reply.

## Security

Upgraded from Next.js 14.2.35 → **15.5.12** to resolve HTTP request deserialization DoS (GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf). `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities.

Greptile Summary

Adds handling for the `.gateway` case to the macOS `DeepLinkHandler.handle(url:)` switch statement to fix a Swift build error. - The `DeepLinkRoute` enum gained a `.gateway(GatewayConnectDeepLink)` case in the shared `OpenClawKit` module - The macOS `DeepLinkHandler` was missing this case, causing a "switch must be exhaustive" compiler error - The fix adds `case .gateway: break` to match the iOS implementation in `NodeAppModel.handleDeepLink` - Gateway deep links are intentionally ignored on macOS (no-op), consistent with iOS behavior

author: thgterto
body:
This PR addresses a High Severity security vulnerability: **Formula Injection (CSV Injection)** in the Google Sheets backend.

### Vulnerability
User input written directly to Google Sheets via `upsertData` was treated as raw cell content. If a malicious user submitted a name or other string field starting with `=`, `@`, `+`, or `-`, Google Sheets would attempt to execute it as a formula. This could lead to data exfiltration (e.g., `=IMPORTXML`) or client-side command execution if exported to CSV/Excel.

### Fix
Implemented a `sanitizeForSheet` function in `backend/GoogleAppsScript.js` that inspects string values before writing. If a value starts with a formula trigger, it prepends a single quote `'` to force the spreadsheet to treat the cell content as text.

### Verification
- **Automated:** Added a new check in `tests/security_checks.py` that statically analyzes `backend/GoogleAppsScript.js` to ensure the sanitization logic is present and used.
- **Manual Verification:** Verified the logic with a standalone test script `tests/verify_gas_sanitization.cjs` (deleted after verification) which confirmed correct escaping behavior for test vectors like `=CMD`, `+123`.

### Impact
- Prevents malicious formula execution in the backend spreadsheet.
- Minimal risk of regression; `sanitizeForSheet` only affects strings starting with specific characters. Normal data remains unchanged.

body:
## Summary

This PR extends the Robot Framework test result archiving system with keyword-level execution tracking and adds Grafana dashboards for visualization. It captures structured test data (answers, grading reasons) via log messages and tracks timing for LLM, safety, and docker keywords.

## Key Changes

- **Keyword-level tracking**: Added `KeywordResult` dataclass and `keyword_results` table to store execution timing for tracked keywords (LLM, safety, docker operations)
- **Structured data capture**: Implemented `RFC_DATA:` prefix convention in log messages to capture test-specific data (actual_answer, expected_answer, grading_reason) without requiring database schema changes
- **Virtual datasets**: Added JOINed SQL views in Superset for cross-table analysis (test_results_detail, model_suite_performance, keyword_timing)
- **Superset dashboards**: Expanded from single dashboard to three specialized dashboards:
  - Test Results: pass rates, model comparison, test breakdown, failures
  - Pipeline Health: pipeline status, duration, queue time, branch/ref analysis
  - Model Analytics: model performance, dry run results, detailed metrics
- **Grafana integration**: Added three new Grafana dashboards with provisioning config:
  - Test Results dashboard with KPIs and trend charts
  - Pipeline Health dashboard with status and performance metrics
  - Keyword Timing dashboard for LLM/keyword execution analysis
- **Enhanced DbListener**: Extended to capture keyword execution via `start_keyword`/`end_keyword` hooks and parse structured log messages
- **Type hints**: Added proper type annotations (`Dict`, `List`, `Any`) throughout

## Implementation Details

author: adammathes
body:
This PR fixes a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability in the `imageProxyHandler` where reading an arbitrarily large response body could lead to memory exhaustion.

🎯 **What:**
- Introduced a 10MB limit (`maxImageProxySize`) for reading proxied image responses.
- Used `io.LimitReader` to enforce this limit, ensuring that only the first 10MB of a response are read into memory.
- Added a regression test `web/proxy_limit_test.go` to verify that large responses are truncated correctly.

⚠️ **Risk:**
- Previously, an attacker could supply a URL to a very large file, causing the server to allocate unbounded memory, potentially crashing the application or the server (OOM).

🛡️ **Solution:**
- By limiting the read size to 10MB, we prevent memory exhaustion attacks via the image proxy. Legitimate images larger than 10MB will be truncated, which is an acceptable trade-off for security.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gravitational/teleport (gravitational/teleport)</summary>

### [`v18.7.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/releases/tag/v18.7.0): Teleport 18.7.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/compare/v18.6.8...v18.7.0)

#### Description

##### Session timeline view for Identity Security

Session player for Identity Security users received an enhanced timeline view with
per-command session breakdown.

##### Organization-level auto-discovery for AWS EC2 instances

AWS auto-discovery supports EC2 instance enrollment from all or a subset of accounts
of an AWS organization without having to configure per-account discovery.

Organization-level discovery for other resources within AWS (RDS, EKS) as well as other
for cloud providers will follow in future releases.

##### Terraform-native flow for configuration of AWS EC2 auto-discovery

Teleport provides in-product UX for configuring EC2 auto-discovery in a single AWS
account using terraform module.

##### Static labels for auto-discovered Windows desktops

Teleport can now be configured to apply a set of static labels to Windows
desktops that it discovers via LDAP. This is an alternative to setting labels
based on the value of LDAP attributes.

##### Access requests privilege escalation UX for AWS

Teleport users are now able to see specific IAM roles available to them when requesting
elevated access to AWS CLI/console. Future releases will extend support for specific
principal selection to access requests for other resource types as well.

##### Entra ID integration status page

Teleport users are now able to see status of the configured Entra ID integration in the
web UI.

##### Inventory UI

Teleport's web UI now includes a new page showing the complete inventory of all instances
and bots connected to the cluster.

##### Managed Updates UI

Teleport's web UI now includes new functionality for working with managed updates.
The UI offers the ability to view and manage the updater configuration as well
as monitor the progress of update rollouts.

##### Split Windows CA

Teleport now introduces a new Windows CA responsible for issuing user certificates for
Windows Desktop access. Currently the User CA issues those certificates, as they are end-user certs.
Splitting the CAs improves Teleport's security posture by introducing a more specialized CA
and allows both CAs to be rotated independently.

##### Other fixes and improvements

- Fixed `tsh kubectl` failing when kubectl flags appear before positional arguments (e.g., `tsh kubectl -n default get pod`). [#​63807](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63807)
- The tsh status command can now be executed in client-only mode with --client. This skips all server-side operations. [#​63786](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63786)
- Improved tracing support via `tsh --trace kubectl`. [#​63762](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63762)
- Added `tctl recordings download` command to download session recordings to local files without requiring direct access to the storage backend. [#​63726](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63726)
- MWI: Add new `tbot start no-op` helper that starts no services. [#​63666](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63666)
- Improved performance and user experience of `teleport backend clone`. [#​63635](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63635)
- Fixed out of sequent audit logs rendering in ui for same timestamp logs. [#​63613](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63613)
- Added the Windows CA, used to issue Windows Desktop Access user certificates. The Windows CA is initially created as a copy of the User CA, so existing trust relationships are maintained. You may rotate either CA in order to create distinct key material (make sure to consult the Certificate Authority Rotation guide before performing a CA rotation). The Windows CA is a top-level CA entity, so it is reflected in all commands that operate on CAs. Updating both command-line tools and Windows Desktop agents is recommended. [#​63547](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/63547)

- Ensure that discovered Windows desktops don't expire when a large discovery interval is configured. [#​62471](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/62471)
- Each Windows desktop `discovery_config` can now include a set of static labels to apply to discovered hosts. [#​62452](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/62452)
- Added support for discovering EC2 instances in all the accounts under an AWS Organization. [#​62302](https://redirect.github.com/gravitational/teleport/pull/62302)

## Summary

- Adds service accounts as machine identities for CI/CD pipelines, independent of human users

- Populates and enforces API token scopes in the auth middleware (previously stored but never checked)
- Full CRUD API for service accounts at `/api/v1/service-accounts` with token management sub-routes

## Changes

**Database (migration 057):**
- `is_service_account` boolean flag on users table with partial index
- `api_token_repositories` join table for per-repo token restrictions
- `created_by_user_id` and `description` columns on api_tokens

**Auth middleware:**
- `AuthExtension` now carries `is_service_account`, `scopes` (populated from DB for API tokens), and `allowed_repo_ids`
- Helper methods: `has_scope()`, `can_access_repo()`, `require_scope()`
- JWT sessions always pass scope checks; API tokens check exact match, `*`, or `admin`

**Service layer:**
- `ApiTokenValidation` struct returned by `validate_api_token` with user + scopes + repo restrictions
- `ServiceAccountService` with create/list/get/update/delete
- Service accounts get `svc-` prefixed usernames, synthetic email, no password, cannot log in interactively

**API handler:**
- 8 admin-only endpoints under `/api/v1/service-accounts`
- Full OpenAPI annotations with `ServiceAccountsApiDoc`

**Note:** The SQLx offline cache (`.sqlx/`) needs regeneration after the migration is applied. Run `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace` against a database with migration 057.

# PR: Implement Reviews & Ratings System (Phase 1: Models) ## Summary Implemented a robust **Review and Rating system** using a **TDD** approach. This phase focuses on the core database schema, rating validations, and integration with the `Product` model for dynamic metrics. Achieved **100% test coverage** for the new module. --- ## Key Features ### 1. Review Infrastructure - **Validated Ratings:** Strict `1-5` star integer validation at both the database and model levels using Django's `MinValueValidator` and `MaxValueValidator`. - **Integrity Constraints:** Enforced `unique_together` on `user` and `product` to prevent multiple reviews from a single user per product. - **Smart Cleanup:** Configured `CASCADE` deletion to ensure data consistency when users or products are removed. - **Optional Feedback:** Designed the `comment` field as an optional text area, allowing for quick star-only ratings. ### 2. Product Integration Added dynamic properties to the `Product` model to provide real-time metrics for the storefront: - **`average_rating`**: Dynamically calculated using Django's `Avg` aggregate, rounded to 1 decimal place. - **`review_count`**: Real-time count of all associated reviews. --- ## TDD & Quality Assurance **13 comprehensive unit tests** were developed following the Red-Green-Refactor cycle: - **Model Integrity (9 tests):** Validates rating bounds, unique constraints, string representations, and relationship behaviors. - **Business Logic (4 tests):** Ensures average rating calculations handle multiple reviews, rounding, and "no-review" scenarios correctly. --- ## Test Results | Metric | Details | | :--- | :--- | | **Total Tests** | 169 (156 existing + 13 new) | | **Pass Rate** | 100% ✅ | | **Coverage** | 100% (Review module) | | **Runtime** | 39.72s | --- ## Technical Implementation ### Database Schema Highlights - **Unique Constraint:** `UNIQUE (user_id, product_id)` - **Check Constraint:** `rating >= 1 AND rating <= 5` - **Indexing:** Optimized for `product_id` and `created_at` for faster storefront loading. --- ## Business Logic Snippet ```python @property def average_rating(self): from django.db.models import Avg result = self.reviews.aggregate(avg=Avg('rating')) return round(result['avg'], 1) if result['avg'] else 0 ``` --- ## Files Changed - `apps/reviews/models.py`: Core Review model and validations. - `apps/products/models.py`: Added rating properties to the Product class. - `tests/reviews/test_review_models.py`: 13 new unit tests. - `tests/factories.py`: Added ReviewFactory for testing. --- ## Next Steps (Phase 2: API) - [ ] Create Review Serializers (handling read/write logic). - [ ] Implement CRUD ViewSets for reviews. - [ ] Add `IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly` permissions. - [ ] Develop 10+ API integration tests. --- ## Status - **Status:** ✅ Ready for Review - **TDD:** ✅ Fully Applied - **Coverage:** 📊 100% (Review Module) ---

Review system foundation complete!
Reliable ratings, enforced integrity, and full test coverage.

This PR adds a Github Action (publish-node-action) that will publish an updated version of your custom node to the [registry](https://registry.comfy.org/) whenever the `pyproject.toml` file changes. The pyproject.toml defines the custom node version you want to publish (added in another PR). Make sure you update the version number in `pyproject.toml` when you make a change that should be published to everyone!

Action Required:

- [ ] Make sure the trigger branch (`master` or `main`) in `publish.yaml` matches the branch you want to use as the publishing branch. It will only trigger when the pyproject.toml gets updated on that branch.
- [ ] Create an api key on the Registry for publishing from Github. [Instructions](https://docs.comfy.org/registry/publishing#create-an-api-key-for-publishing).
- [ ] Add it to your Github Repository Secrets as `REGISTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

body:
## Summary - **Problem:** `runGatewayUpdate()` runs `npm i -g` (or pnpm/bun equivalent) without checking write permissions first. Package managers remove the existing install before writing the new one, so an EACCES failure mid-install leaves the CLI partially deleted with no rollback. - **Why it matters:** The gateway becomes a zombie — process stays alive but the underlying code is gone. Messages are silently dropped. We discovered this after a real-world **34-hour silent outage** caused by a permission misconfiguration. - **What changed:** Added a single `fs.access(pkgRoot, W_OK)` pre-check before the destructive global install step. If the directory is not writable, the update returns early with `status: "error"` and `reason: "no-write-permission"` — no install attempt, no damage. - **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No behavior change for working installs. No refactoring. Git-based update paths are untouched. The existing global install logic is identical when permissions are fine. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Related #9100 (npm global update drops bundled deps) - Related #6318 (npm global upgrade path is fragile) - Related #11237 (Gateway Uninstalled on Restart) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - When `update.run` detects the global install directory is not writable, it now returns `{ status: "error", reason: "no-write-permission" }` instead of attempting the install and potentially destroying the existing installation. - No change for users with correct permissions — behavior is identical. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the npm/pnpm/bun install command is *prevented* from running, not changed - Data access scope changed? `No` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: Linux (GCP, x64) - Runtime/container: Node v22.22.0, npm global install - Model/provider: N/A (infra bug) - Integration/channel: All channels affected (gateway-level) - Relevant config: Global npm install at `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw` owned by root, gateway running as non-root user ### Steps 1. Install OpenClaw globally: `sudo npm i -g openclaw` 2. Run gateway as non-root user 3. Trigger update: `update.run` (via cron, weekly update job, or manual) 4. npm tries `npm i -g openclaw@latest`, hits EACCES, partially removes existing install 5. Gateway continues running but all tool execution / message handling breaks silently ### Expected - Update detects missing write permission and returns a clear error *before* touching the filesystem ### Actual (before fix) - npm begins uninstalling the old version, hits EACCES writing the new version, leaves a corrupted half-deleted install ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after - Added test: "returns error with no-write-permission when global install path is not writable" - All 16 tests in `update-runner.test.ts` pass (including the new one) - Linter clean (oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors) ## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: Ran `vitest run src/infra/update-runner.test.ts` — all 16 tests pass. Test uses `fs.chmod(pkgRoot, 0o555)` to simulate a non-writable global install directory. - Edge cases checked: Ensured the check uses `W_OK` on the package root directory itself (not parent), which matches where npm/pnpm/bun need to write. Verified `fs.constants.W_OK` is available on `node:fs/promises`. - What I did **not** verify: Full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` suite (ran only the affected test file). Did not test on Windows (EACCES semantics differ). ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `No` - Migration needed? `No` ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks) - How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert this single commit - Files/config to restore: None - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: If the W_OK check gives false negatives (reports not writable when it is), updates would be blocked with `no-write-permission`. User can verify by checking `ls -la` on the global install path. ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: On some platforms, `fs.access(dir, W_OK)` may not perfectly predict whether `npm i -g` will succeed (e.g., ACLs, SELinux, Windows) - Mitigation: This is a best-effort pre-check. False negatives (blocking a valid update) are much less harmful than the current behavior (destroying the install). Users hitting a false negative get a clear error with the specific path to investigate. --- 🤖 *AI-assisted PR (Claude via OpenClaw agent). Fully tested. The humans understand the code.*

Greptile Summary

Adds a write-permission pre-check (`fs.access(pkgRoot, W_OK)`) before the destructive `npm i -g` / `pnpm` / `bun` global install step in `runGatewayUpdate()`. This prevents the package manager from partially deleting the existing installation when it hits EACCES mid-install, which previously caused a 34-hour silent outage where the gateway stayed alive but all tool execution and message handling broke. - `update-runner.ts`: Inserts a `try { await fs.access(pkgRoot, fs.constants.W_OK) }` check immediately after detecting the global install manager but before any install commands run. On failure, returns `{ status: "error", reason: "no-write-permission" }` with zero steps executed. - `update-runner.test.ts`: Adds a test using `fs.chmod(pkgRoot, 0o555)` to simulate a non-writable directory, verifying the error return and confirming the install command is never invoked. Permissions are properly restored in a `finally` block. - The change is minimal and well-scoped — no behavior change for working installs, no refactoring, git-based update paths untouched.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it adds a defensive pre-check with no behavior change for working installs. - The change is minimal (17 lines of production code), well-tested, correctly typed against UpdateRunResult, and properly integrated with existing consumers. The pre-check is a strict improvement: it prevents a destructive failure mode with no downside for correct-permission scenarios. The fs.access/W_OK API is well-established in Node.js and already used elsewhere in this codebase. - No files require special attention. author: drugsprojectvit-lgtm
body:
### Motivation
- Split the monolithic ingestion -> parse -> embed -> graph -> query pipeline into clearer production-ready components to enable async ingestion, incremental indexing, and scalable storage.
- Replace fragile hand-written Tree-sitter walks with query-driven extraction to reduce maintenance surface and make it easy to add new languages via `.scm` files.
- Move heavy LLM work off the ingestion path by turning file summarization into a cheap signature-first approach and making full LLM overviews on-demand to cut cost and latency.
- Replace in-memory/JSON graph persistence with a persistent graph adapter and add a pluggable vector adapter to prepare for real graph/vector databases.

### Description
- Introduced a queued ingestion pipeline and provider abstraction by adding `SourceProvider` (abstract), `LocalSource`, `GitSource`, and a small `IngestionJobQueue` that enqueues and processes ingestion jobs via `ingest_sources`/`process_ingestion_jobs`, and computes per-file hashes for incremental indexing, and added `JOB_QUEUE_FILE` config.
- Reworked parsing to be query-driven by adding `TreeSitterQueryRegistry`, loading `.scm` query files in `queries/`, and a generic `_extract_symbols_with_queries` extraction path that falls back to the previous extractors when needed.
- Implemented lazy, low-cost summarization in `ProjectSummarizer` so ingestion records signature-style file summaries by default and performs LLM-based project overviews only when `force_llm=True`.
- Added production-oriented adapters: `GraphStorageService` (SQLite-backed tables `functions`/`calls` with `upsert_repo_graph` and `impact_analysis`) and `HybridVectorStoreService` (pluggable local-backed records persisted to `VECTOR_DB_FILE`), and wired both into `build_multi_symbol_graph` to persist incremental graph and vector records.
- Added infrastructure and config: `JOB_QUEUE_FILE`, `GRAPH_DB_FILE`, `VECTOR_DB_FILE`, `TREE_SITTER_QUERY_DIR`, and created sample query files `queries/{python,javascript,typescript,go}.scm` to support query-driven parsing.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m py_compile github.py` to verify syntax and the file compiles successfully (success).
- Performed a smoke import attempt `python - <<'PY'\nimport github\n...\nPY` which failed in the environment due to a missing external dependency (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git'`), noted as an environment setup issue rather than a code error (fail - missing dependency).
- Created and validated Tree-sitter query files under `queries/` and confirmed the new query registry and parsing code paths are present and integrated by running the compile check above (success).

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces comprehensive unit test coverage, internationalization (i18n) support for English and Ukrainian, and refactors core analytics and utility functions into reusable, well-tested modules. The codebase is now more maintainable, testable, and user-friendly with multi-language support.

## Key Changes

### Testing Infrastructure
- Added **114 test cases** across 4 new test files covering:
  - `analytics.ts`: KPI calculations (delivery rates, on-time counts, method categorization)
  - `dateUtils.ts`: Date parsing and comparison with multiple format support
  - `deliveryMethods.ts`: Delivery method detection and normalization
  - `statuses.ts`: Status classification (delivered/undelivered)
- Configured Vitest in `vite.config.ts` with proper TypeScript support
- Added test scripts to `package.json` (`test` and `test:ci`)

### Internationalization (i18n)
- Integrated `react-i18next` for multi-language support
- Created translation files for **English** (`en.json`) and **Ukrainian** (`ua.json`)
- Translated all UI strings: KPI labels, chart titles, sidebar navigation, filter labels, and app messages
- Updated components to use `useTranslation()` hook throughout the dashboard

### Core Refactoring & New Utilities
- **`constants/statuses.ts`**: Centralized status classification with `isDelivered()` and `isUndelivered()` predicates
- **`constants/deliveryMethods.ts`**: Delivery method detection with support for hand delivery, safe place, and post office variants (English & Ukrainian keywords)
- **`constants/chartTheme.ts`**: Extracted chart styling logic for consistent dark/light mode theming
- **`utils/dateUtils.ts`**: Robust date parsing supporting `dd.MM.yyyy`, `dd/MM/yyyy`, and `dd-MM-yyyy` formats with `parseDate()`, `isSameDay()`, and `compareDates()` utilities
- **`hooks/useThemeMode.ts`**: Custom hook for theme state management

### Schema & Data Validation
- Updated `DeliveryRecordSchema` to use optional string defaults (`optStr`) for all fields, improving CSV parsing robustness
- Enhanced `csvParser.ts` to return `ParseResult` with warnings array for better error reporting
- Added validation against Zod schema with graceful error handling

### UI & Component Improvements
- **`FilterBar.tsx`**: New filter component supporting date range, city, and courier filtering with Redux integration
- **`ErrorBoundary.tsx`**: Error boundary component for graceful error handling in chart sections
- Updated `Dashboard.tsx` to use filtered records via Redux selectors and display filter bar
- Refactored chart components (`TrendChart`, `RegionalChart`, `DensityChart`, `CourierChart`, `MethodChart`) to use centralized theme utilities and i18n
- Updated `Sidebar.tsx` and `Header.tsx` with i18n support and routing integration

### Redux Enhancements
- Added `store/selectors.ts` with memoized selectors:
  - `selectFilteredRecords`: Applies date range, city, and courier filters
  - `selectUniqueCities` and `selectUniqueCouriers`: Extract unique values for filter dropdowns
- Created `filtersSlice` for managing filter state (date range, city, courier)

### Analytics Refactoring
- Updated `analytics.ts` to use new utility functions (`isDelivered`, `isUndelivered`, `isHandDelivery`, `isSafePlace`, `isSameDay`)
- Improved on-time delivery calculation using parsed dates instead of string comparison
- Enhanced safe place detection logic to avoid false positives

### Routing & Navigation
- Added `BrowserRouter` to `main.tsx` for multi-page support
- Updated `App.tsx` with route definitions for `/dashboard` and `/import` pages
- Created `ImportPage` component for empty state with data import prompt

### Styling & UX
- Updated `index.css` to support light mode by default with dark mode override
- Removed unused `App.css` and `react.svg`

author: gabrielrinaldi
body:
## Summary
When running OpenClaw as a system-level systemd service (e.g. on NixOS with a dedicated `openclaw` user), the user D-Bus session is unavailable. This causes `openclaw status` to incorrectly report "systemd not installed" and breaks all daemon management commands.

This PR adds a `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_SYSTEM=1` environment variable that switches all `systemctl` calls from `--user` to system scope.

## Changes

- **`src/daemon/systemd.ts`**: Add `isSystemLevelService()` and `systemctlScope()` helpers. All 14 `--user` call sites now go through `systemctlScope()`. Availability checks handle exit code 3 (no units loaded) as success for system-level services. Unit path resolves to `/etc/systemd/system/` instead of `~/.config/systemd/user/`.
- **`src/commands/systemd-linger.ts`**: Skip linger management when running as system service (not applicable).
- **`src/daemon/systemd.test.ts`**: Add tests for `isSystemLevelService`, system-level availability, and system-level unit path resolution.

## Usage

```bash
# In your systemd service environment or shell profile:
export OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_SYSTEM=1
export OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw  # if unit name differs from default
openclaw status  # now correctly detects system-level service
```

Works alongside the existing `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT` env var for custom unit names.

## AI assisted

Driven and tested by me, but AI assisted on finding all places that needed change. Changes were discussed and reviewed by me. Although this is not my primary coding language. 

## Testing

- All 18 tests in src/daemon/systemd.test.ts pass
- TypeScript typecheck clean (no new errors)
- Tested on NixOS with system-level openclaw.service running as dedicated user

## Non related changes

I had to include:
- apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift
- apps/macos/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift

So CI would pass, this seems like something is missing upstream and not part of my changes

body:
### Motivation
- The generated `agent.py` contained a Windows path literal that caused `SyntaxError` when piped into PowerShell (`iwr ... | iex`).
- The Windows installer reported "Instalación completa" and created a scheduled task even when enrollment failed, leading to broken agent installs.
- The install UI used the loopback `server_url` by default which can mislead users installing on remote hosts.

### Description
- Updated `build_agent_py()` to compute the Windows disk root from `SystemDrive` and build `disk_target` as `system_drive + "\\"` instead of a raw trailing-backslash literal (file: `agents/views.py`).
- Hardened the generated Windows installer (`build_windows_installer()` in `agents/views.py`) to: validate `agent.py` with `python -m py_compile` and abort on syntax errors, abort if `--enroll` returns a non-zero exit, avoid creating/starting scheduled tasks on failure, and only print the success message when all steps succeed; added clearer error messages and log/path hints.
- Made the UI install page detect loopback hosts and show a hint to replace `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` with the server IP/DNS when installing on another machine, and added the same note to the troubleshooting list (files: `agents/templates/agents/install.html`, `agents/views.py`).
- Added a short deployment note to `README.md` advising to restart the Django server after changing the script-generation logic so the updated installer is served.
- Added unit tests `agents/tests/test_agent_download_scripts.py` to verify the `disk_target` fix, presence and order of the fail-fast checks in the generated PowerShell installer, and the loopback hint rendering.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m py_compile agents/views.py agents/tests/test_agent_download_scripts.py` which succeeded and validated Python syntax for the modified files.
- Attempted `python manage.py test ...` but test execution failed because the environment lacked `djangorestframework` and `pip install -r requirements.txt` could not fetch packages due to network/proxy restrictions, so full Django test run was not possible.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a local-first, single-household monthly fiscal dashboard with strict TypeScript, deterministic build, and Prisma-backed persistence using the mandated Fiscal model naming. 
- Seed the app from two CSV exports and expose thin, Zod-validated APIs and small service-layer modules to keep boundaries explicit and auditable. 
- Ensure all write operations are transactional and logged (AuditEvent) for traceability and idempotency. 

### Description
- Added the exact locked Prisma schema (FiscalYear, FiscalMonth, Group, LineItem, ExpectedOverride, Transaction, Settings, AuditEvent), a SQLite migration scaffold, and a Prisma client singleton wrapper at `src/lib/db/prisma.ts`. 
- Implemented idempotent seeding (`prisma/seed.ts`) that builds the current fiscal year/months and seeds Groups/LineItems from CSVs using a reusable CSV parser (`src/lib/seed/parseBudgetCsv.ts`) and currency utilities (`src/lib/utils/currency.ts`). 
- Introduced a clear service layer with transactional write flows and audit logging: `fiscalService`, `transactionService`, `catalogService`, `expectedService`, and `rollupService` with helper tests for rollups and CSV parsing under `src/lib/*/__tests__`. 
- Built thin Zod-validated API routes for active fiscal context, transactions, groups, line-items, and expected-overrides under `src/app/api/*`, and created a Tailwind-based `/dashboard` page plus small chart and top-bar components for the MVP UI. 
- Added project scaffolding (Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind + Chart.js + Vitest), dev/build/test scripts in `package.json`, `.env.example`, CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), migration SQL scaffold and structured run logs under `logs/`.

## Summary

## Changes

- **What**: The `ci-lint-format` workflow uses `secrets.PR_GH_TOKEN` for checkout. The fix uses `github.token` as a fallback for fork PRs — this is always available with read-only access, which is sufficient since the workflow already skips commit/push for forks.
