### Motivation
- Provide a median-carry based gapping ladder so users can diagnose bag spacing (overlap, compressed gaps, large cliffs) from a single session.
- Use robust per-club statistics (median, P10/P90, IQR-based outlier tagging) to avoid noisy decisions from outliers or small samples.
- Surface actionable diagnostics and human-readable warnings in the uploader UI so parsing and gapping issues are visible immediately.

### Description
- Added gapping data model and engine to `lib/r10.ts` including `GapStatus`, `GappingRow`, `GappingInsight`, `GappingLadder`, `buildGappingLadder`, and supporting helpers (`getClubFamily`, `classifyGap`, `buildGapWarning`, quantile/stdDev helpers, and ordering utilities). 
- Extended import/normalization in `lib/r10.ts` to preserve `clubType`/`clubName`/`clubModel`, robust header alias matching, locale-aware numeric coercion, IQR outlier tagging, and `buildImportReport` for column/club/warning diagnostics.
- Wired the uploader UI (`components/csv-uploader.tsx`) to compute and render the new Gapping Ladder section (median/P10–P90, gap-to-next, status badges, per-row warnings, and top-level insights) and added an import diagnostics panel and outlier toggle.
- Added visual styles for insight severities and gap-status badges in `app/globals.css`, created `docs/sprint2-part-a.md`, updated `README.md` links, and included a sample screenshot artifact demonstrating the ladder.

## Summary
This PR adds automated deployment to GitHub Pages using GitHub Actions, enabling continuous deployment of the repository contents to a GitHub Pages site.

## Key Changes
- **Added GitHub Actions workflow** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`): Automated deployment pipeline that triggers on pushes to the `main` branch or manual workflow dispatch
  - Checks out the repository code
  - Configures GitHub Pages environment
  - Uploads repository contents as a deployment artifact
  - Deploys to GitHub Pages using the official deployment action
  
- **Added `.nojekyll` file**: Disables Jekyll processing for GitHub Pages, allowing the site to be served as-is without Jekyll transformation

- The workflow uses GitHub's official actions for Pages configuration and deployment (`actions/configure-pages@v5` and `actions/deploy-pages@v4`)
- Appropriate permissions are configured for the workflow (contents read, pages write, id-token write)
- Concurrency is set to prevent simultaneous deployments
- The entire repository (`.`) is uploaded as the deployment artifact, making all contents available on the GitHub Pages site

- **Controller (Python)**  
  - Watches annotated K8s resources, reconciles tabs with the Organizr API (v2), supports upsert/sync policies.  
  - Structured logging (structlog), config via env (Pydantic), API key from Secret or file.  
  - Security defaults: non-root, read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation.

- **Helm chart**  
  - Wraps [bjw-s app-template](https://bjw-s-labs.github.io/helm-charts/docs/app-template/) with security-hardened defaults.  
  - RBAC (ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding); **HPA off by default** (set `hpa.enabled: true` for 1–3 replicas). No ingress or persistence.  
  - All `ORGANIZR_*` env vars documented in values comments and [helm/README.md](helm/README.md). Image default: Docker Hub (`docker.io/expectedbehaviors/organizr-tab-controller`); override for GHCR or other registries as needed.  
  - Resource requests/limits tuned for headroom (256Mi/500m limits) so the controller won’t OOM under load.

- **Docker**  
  - Multi-stage build on Chainguard Python (distroless runtime, non-root).  
  - Image built and published by GitHub Actions on release and on push to `main` (Docker Hub).

- **CI/CD**  
  - **Release on merge to main**: bumps patch version, creates tag and GitHub Release.  
  - **Docker build and publish**: on release and on `main` path changes.  
  - **Helm chart publish**: packages chart with version-matched image tag, uploads `.tgz` to the release.  
  - **Release notes from PR**: OpenAI summarizes merged PR into bullet points (**requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`**; job fails if unset).  
  - Single CI/CD doc: [.github/workflows/README.md](.github/workflows/README.md) (credentials, triggers, release flow). No separate docs folder.

## Paradigm alignment

- **Feature branch**: Changes via this branch; no direct commits to `main`.  
- **Security**: Non-root, minimal capabilities, no ingress for the controller.  
- **Deployment**: Chart suitable for Argo CD or Helm; API key from Secret; image registry aligned with Docker Hub workflow.  
- **User-friendly**: All env vars documented in Helm chart and root README; HPA off by default; resource limits forgiving.

## Pre-merge review notes

- Image repository in chart defaults to Docker Hub; override `image.repository` when using GHCR or another registry.  
- Leader-election settings in config are reserved for future HA; not yet implemented.  
- Signal handling in the entrypoint is robust to non-standard signal numbers.

## Docs

- **README.md** – project overview, annotations, config, development, Organizr links.  
- **helm/README.md** – Helm/Argo CD install, **Environment variables** table, values.  
- **.github/workflows/README.md** – CI/CD only (workflows, required secrets: Docker Hub, OpenAI).

body:
## Summary

Add 33 property-based and edge-case tests in `crates/graphcal-eval/tests/edge_case_bugs.rs` to stress-test the evaluation engine on areas critical to engineering users.

## Bug found

**`to_int()` silently saturates for out-of-range float values** (tracked in #85):
- `to_int(1e20)` silently returns `i64::MAX` instead of an error
- `to_int(-1e20)` silently returns `i64::MIN` instead of an error
- Any float outside `[i64::MIN, i64::MAX]` produces a wrong value with no warning

This is critical for a safety-focused engineering language. 5 tests are `#[ignore]`d pending the fix.

## Tests added (28 passing, 5 ignored)

Areas covered:
- **Integer arithmetic overflow**: boundary values for `checked_add/sub/mul/pow/neg`
- **Float power edge cases**: `0.0^0.0`, negative bases with integer/fractional exponents
- **Float division**: `-0.0` divisor handling
- **Range index step counts**: floating-point precision with 0.1, 0.25, 0.3 step sizes
- **Unit conversions**: round-trip `km -> km`, compound units `km/hour`, `km^2`
- **Type conversions**: `to_int` range checking, `to_float` precision
- **Aggregation functions**: `sum()`, `mean()` on indexed collections
- **Commutativity**: integer and float `+` and `*` (proptest)
- **Euclidean identity**: `a == (a / b) * b + (a % b)` (proptest)
- **Float equality semantics**: documents `0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3` behavior

## Other changes

- `.gitignore`: add `**/*.proptest-regressions` pattern

author: gsinghjay
body:
## Summary

This PR adds **individual sponsor detail pages** so visitors can click on a sponsor card and see their full profile. It also adds a **breadcrumb navigation component** that shows where you are on the site (e.g., Home > Sponsors > Acme Corp).

### What was added

- **Sponsor detail page** (`/sponsors/[slug]`) — each sponsor in Sanity gets their own page showing:
  - Full-size logo (200x200)
  - Company name with tier badge (gold, silver, etc.)
  - Industry, description, and website link
  - An "Associated Projects" section (empty for now — will show projects once Epic 4 is built)
  - A "Back to Sponsors" link to return to the listing page
- **Breadcrumb component** — a reusable navigation helper that shows the page hierarchy (Home > Sponsors > Sponsor Name). This will also be reused for project detail pages later.
- **Two new GROQ queries** in `sanity.ts`:
  - `ALL_SPONSOR_SLUGS_QUERY` — fetches all sponsor slugs so Astro can generate a static page for each one at build time
  - `SPONSOR_BY_SLUG_QUERY` — fetches a single sponsor's full data by their URL slug

### How it works

Astro uses a feature called `getStaticPaths()` to generate one HTML page per sponsor at **build time** (not at runtime). When you visit `/sponsors/acme-corporation`, you're loading a pre-built HTML file — no API calls happen in the browser.

The breadcrumb is split into two `.astro` files (`Breadcrumb.astro` + `BreadcrumbItem.astro`) because Astro's template parser has trouble with conditional rendering (ternary expressions) inside `.map()` loops. This is a known Astro limitation, and splitting into a sub-component is the clean workaround.

### Key patterns used (from previous stories)

- `stegaClean()` on all href values — prevents Visual Editing stega characters from corrupting URLs
- `urlFor()` with the `as unknown as Parameters<typeof urlFor>[0]` cast — needed because GROQ-dereferenced image assets have a different shape than what `@sanity/image-url` expects
- `tierStyles` record duplicated locally (same 5 lines as SponsorCard) — intentionally not extracted to a shared file since only 2 consumers exist

## Test plan

- [x] 6 Breadcrumb component tests (Container API) — nav element, ordered list, links, aria-current, separators
- [x] 3 GROQ query string tests — verify new queries target correct types and fields
- [x] 2 `getSponsorBySlug()` functional tests — verifies fetch params and null handling
- [x] Typed test fixture (`sponsor-detail.ts`) with full and minimal sponsor data
- [x] `npm run build` generates all 7 sponsor detail HTML files
- [x] `npm run test:unit` — 407 tests pass, zero regressions

author: pspoerri
body:
## Summary

This branch delivers a comprehensive set of performance improvements to the GeoTIFF-to-PMTiles pipeline, targeting memory usage, CPU hot paths, tile I/O, and output quality.

### Memory & I/O pipeline
- **Lock-free tile reads** — `ioLoop` now owns its temp file exclusively; readers access it through an `atomic.Pointer`, eliminating RWMutex contention between the writer goroutine and concurrent tile readers.
- **Encoded in-memory storage** — Worker threads release raw pixel data immediately after encoding. `DiskTileStore` keeps non-uniform tiles in their compressed form (PNG/WebP/JPEG) in memory, reducing per-tile footprint from 64-256 KB to ~10-50 KB (5-25x reduction).
- **Backpressure-based memory limits** — `Put()` blocks via `sync.Cond` when memory exceeds `MemoryLimitBytes`, preventing unbounded growth when workers outpace disk spilling.
- **Tile deduplication in PMTiles writer** — Identical tile data (common with uniform/ocean tiles) is written to disk once; subsequent entries reuse the offset via FNV-64a hashing. Temp files are now created in the output directory instead of system temp.

### CPU hot-path optimizations (24% wall-time, 43% CPU reduction)
- Replace `math.Pow(2, z)` with bit-shift `pow2()` across all coordinate transforms.
- Switch `TileCache` shard locks from `sync.Mutex` to `sync.RWMutex` for concurrent reads.
- Batch bilinear pixel reads: 1 cache lookup per output pixel instead of 4.
- Bypass `image.YCbCr` bounds checking with direct slice access and inline color conversion.
- Precompute per-tile lon/lat arrays, reducing trig calls from O(n^2) to O(n).
- Move `clampByte` to package level for compiler inlining; use direct `Pix` slice writes.

### Lanczos-3 resampling (new default)
- Full Lanczos-3 (sinc-windowed sinc, 6x6 kernel) implementation for both per-pixel reprojection and pyramid downsampling, replacing bilinear as the default.
- Optimized with batched tile fetches (36 cache lookups down to 1-4), precomputed sin LUT, and YCbCr-specialized fast paths — achieving 4.7x speedup over the naive implementation.
- Dedicated quadrant downsamplers for RGBA, grayscale, and Terrarium elevation paths.

### Documentation
- New `ARCHITECTURE.md` describing the render pipeline and data flow.
- `README.md` updated with performance section, Lanczos flag documentation, and profiling findings.
- Results files with detailed profiling data for Lanczos implementation and optimization.

## Changed files

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| CLI | `cmd/geotiff2pmtiles/main.go` |
| Tile store | `internal/tile/diskstore.go`, `internal/tile/generator.go` |
| Resampling | `internal/tile/resample.go`, `internal/tile/downsample.go` |
| PMTiles writer | `internal/pmtiles/writer.go`, `internal/pmtiles/header.go`, `internal/pmtiles/writer_test.go` |
| Tile cache | `internal/cog/tilecache.go` |
| Coordinates | `internal/coord/mercator.go` |
| Benchmarks | `internal/tile/bench_test.go` |
| Docs | `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `results/` |

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` passes (including new `TestWriter_Deduplication` test)
- [x] Benchmark comparison: `go test -bench=. ./internal/tile/ ./internal/pmtiles/`
- [x] End-to-end conversion of a multi-band GeoTIFF with `--resampling lanczos` (default) produces visually sharp pyramid tiles
- [x] Verify memory stays bounded under `--memory-limit` with a large input file
- [x] Confirm deduplication: PMTiles header `NumTileContents < NumAddressedTiles` for datasets with uniform regions
- [x] Regression check: `--resampling bilinear` and `--resampling nearest` still work correctly

body:
## Problem

MAT Waves 5.5, 5.6, 5.7 closed with 100% GREEN tests despite missing critical deliverables: React app scaffolding, UI-to-API wiring, Supabase deployment. Architecture specified these components; implementation omitted them. Wave gates validated test pass rates but not deliverable existence.

## Changes

### New Canon: `WAVES_5_TO_7_INFRA_FE_WIRING_LESSONS.md` (22KB, PUBLIC_API)

Documents cross-wave failure patterns and prevention measures:

**4 Systemic Patterns Identified**:
1. Missing deliverable detection failure (gates check tests, not artifacts)
2. "Tests pass" ≠ "System works" conflation  
3. Deployment deferred as separate concern
4. Architecture completeness unenforced at implementation

**Prevention Measures**:
- Pre-wave infrastructure validation (deployment platforms configured before authorization)
- Physical deliverable verification (file existence + launchability checks)
- Deployment URL documentation (working frontend/backend URLs required)
- E2E tests against deployed environments (not localhost)

### Template Updates

**`minimum-architecture-template.md`** - 3 new mandatory sections:
- **4.1.1 Infrastructure Deployment Validation**: Pre-wave checklist for frontend/backend/database provisioning

body:
Button variants (.btn, .btn.primary, .btn.ghost) had inconsistent heights (34px-46.6px) due to inherited line-height values from browser defaults. This caused visual misalignment in action button rows throughout the site.

## Changes

Added explicit `line-height: 1.4` to all button style definitions:

- **style.css** - Base `.btn` class
- **7 demo pages** - Custom button style overrides (tabular-risk, visual-inspector, vision-classifier, forecast-dashboard, doc-classifier, edgepulse, infra-template)

```css
.btn{
  display:inline-flex;
  align-items:center;
  /* ... */
  font-size: 14px;
  line-height: 1.4;  /* Added for consistent height calculation */
  /* ... */
}
```

## Result

All button variants now render with uniform heights (~37.6px on main pages, ~41.6-44.8px on demo pages), ensuring perfect alignment in action rows while preserving all existing visual styling.

## UI/UX Description

1. **Color Selection**: Choose an appropriate shade of blue that aligns with the app's branding and accessibility standards. Recommended starting point: a mid-range blue such as `#1E3A8A` (deep navy for a professional feel), `#2563EB` (vivid brand blue), or `#DBEAFE` (light sky blue for subtle backgrounds) — the exact shade should be confirmed with the design team or stakeholder.

5. **Transitions**: If the theme is toggled dynamically, a smooth CSS transition (`transition: background-color 0.3s ease`) should be applied to prevent jarring visual snaps.

6. **Responsive Behavior**: The blue background must render consistently across all viewport sizes — mobile, tablet, and desktop — with no white gaps, overflow artifacts, or unintended fallback colors on scroll or overscroll bounce effects.

7. **Visual Consistency**: Ensure scroll areas, sidebars, headers, footers, and modals are all considered so no element retains an inconsistent or conflicting background color.

author: iduartgomez
body:
## Summary
This PR replaces several `panic!()` calls with proper error logging and graceful error handling throughout the codebase. This improves the robustness of the system by preventing crashes and allowing errors to be logged and handled appropriately.

## Key Changes
- **Native API logging functions** (`log::info`, `rand::rand_bytes`, `time::utc_now`): Replaced panics on unset module IDs with `tracing::error!()` calls and early returns, allowing the system to continue operating instead of crashing
- **Client event combinator**: Replaced panic on unhandled client errors with error logging and a break statement to exit the loop gracefully
- **Contract executor**: Replaced bare `panic!()` in `unwrap_request()` with `unreachable!()` macro and a descriptive message for better error diagnostics

## Implementation Details
- All panic replacements maintain the original error context through descriptive log messages
- Early returns and loop breaks ensure the system can recover from these error conditions
- The `unreachable!()` macro in the executor provides better compile-time guarantees while still documenting the impossible state

author: copilot
body:
Pentest identified 6 vulnerabilities (2 critical architectural, 4 medium) plus opportunities for active defense. The password reset deleted the hash creating a race window, auth used client-side SHA-256 hashes as tokens (pass-the-hash), admin tokens lived in localStorage (XSS-stealable), image proxy was vulnerable to DNS rebinding, analytics had no cardinality cap, and KV reads used a bypassable deny-list.

## Critical: Auth architecture rewrite

- **Server-side password hashing** — New `api/auth.js` with `crypto.scrypt` + random salt. Client never hashes passwords. Legacy SHA-256 hashes auto-migrate on successful login.
- **HttpOnly session cookies** — Replace `localStorage` admin-token with `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookies. Session tokens are random 256-bit values stored in KV with 24h TTL. JavaScript cannot read them.
- **Password reset race condition** — `kv.del('admin-password-hash')` replaced with `randomBytes(32)` token stored with 10-min TTL. Hash is never deleted. Confirm flow accepts `{token, newPassword}` and hashes server-side.

```js
// Before: attacker wins the race between del() and user setting new password
await kv.del('admin-password-hash') // window of vulnerability

// After: hash stays intact, reset requires a cryptographic token
const token = randomBytes(32).toString('hex')
await kv.set('admin-reset-token', token, { ex: 600 })
```

## High: KV read allow-list

Deny-list (`includes('token') || includes('secret')`) replaced with explicit allow-list. Only `band-data` is publicly readable; all other keys require a valid session.

## Medium: DNS rebinding, analytics DoS, drive-folder privacy

- **DNS rebinding** — `dns.promises.resolve4/resolve6` (parallelized) checks all resolved IPs against private ranges before `fetch`. Blocks TOCTOU attacks where DNS returns safe IP during hostname check but private IP during fetch.
- **Analytics DoS** — User-controlled values normalized to bounded sets (referrers→domains, devices/browsers→known enums, screen res→validated format). Global `HLEN` cap at 2000 fields.
- **Drive-folder privacy** — Images routed through `/api/image-proxy?url=<encoded wsrv.nl URL>` so visitor IPs never reach third-party services. wsrv.nl still handles resizing.

## Active defenses

- **Wfuzz/scanner tarpit** — Suspicious User-Agent patterns (Wfuzz, Nikto, sqlmap, etc.) trigger 3-5s artificial delay + `{"error": "NOOB_DETECTED"}` response.
- **Honeypot maze** — `api/admin/logs/[id].js` generates infinite paginated fake log entries with 2-5s tarpit per request. Scanners exhaust memory/time crawling non-existent data.

## Scope

19 files changed (12 modified, 2 new), 193 tests passing, 0 CodeQL alerts. Logout button wired up in EditControls.

author: delanni
body:
## Summary
In our auto-generated moon confgis, the `@group(src)` is generated off the tsconfig's prescriptions on included files. For non-ts projects, configuration projects or odd ones, this doesn't exist. Since we already had some tasks referring to `src` groups, we were occasionally getting errors, e.g. for when we're querying.

This PR generates a `src` group for every package - if included files are not prescribed in a tsconfig file, it will glob for any source files within the package. Maybe not the best/most sophisticated query for source files (e.g.: it includes configs too) but for config projects this is accurate.

This will enable us to run `moon query projects` without an error.

cc: @tylersmalley

author: tiulpin
body:
## Description

Ran `go fix ./...` to modernize the codebase with idiomatic Go patterns introduced in recent Go versions. This is a purely mechanical, zero-behavior-change refactoring across 20 files.

## What changed

### `interface{}` → `any` (Go 1.18)
`any` has been the built-in alias for `interface{}` since Go 1.18. Updated all occurrences of `map[string]interface{}` and `...interface{}` variadic params to use the idiomatic `any` form.

### `strings.HasPrefix` + `TrimPrefix` → `strings.CutPrefix` (Go 1.20)
Combines the prefix check and trim into a single call, eliminating redundant string scanning.

### Manual contains loops → `slices.Contains` (Go 1.21)
Replaced hand-written `for range` contains checks with the standard library `slices.Contains`. Cleaner and less error-prone.

### Manual min logic → builtin `min` (Go 1.21)
Replaced `if x > y { x = y }` patterns with the builtin `min()` function.

### `[]byte(fmt.Sprintf(...))` → `fmt.Appendf(nil, ...)` (Go 1.19)
Avoids an intermediate string allocation when the result is `[]byte`.

### `strings.Split` → `strings.SplitSeq` (Go 1.24)
Returns an iterator instead of allocating a `[]string` slice — more memory-efficient when you only need to iterate once.

### String concatenation → `strings.Builder`
Uses `strings.Builder` instead of repeated `+=` concatenation in a loop.

#### Why `go fix` is cool
https://go.dev/blog/gofix


## Types of changes

- [x] Docs change / refactoring / dependency upgrade

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.

body:
The "Stop All Scans" button sets scan process globals to `None` but running threads never checked for this signal.

## Changes

Added stop signal checks at the start of each scan loop iteration:

- **Missing releases scan** (line 2492)
- **Navidrome scan** (line 7010)
- **Combined scan** (line 7120)

Each check acquires `scan_lock`, tests if the process variable is `None`, writes "stopped" status to progress file, and returns.

```python
for idx, (artist_name, info) in enumerate(artists[start_idx:], start=start_idx+1):
    # Check if scan should stop
    with scan_lock:
        if scan_process_combined is None:
            logging.info("Combined scan stop signal received, exiting gracefully")
            _write_progress_with_current_artist(combined_progress_file, "combined_scan", False, {"status": "stopped", "exit_code": 0})
            return
    
    # ... process artist
```

## Limitations

Scans that delegate to external modules (popularity, singles, beets) cannot be stopped mid-operation without modifying those modules. They will complete their current operation before respecting the stop signal.

author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary
This change refactors the application to use per-session git repositories instead of a single shared git repository. Each session now gets its own isolated git directory, improving session isolation and enabling independent git identity configuration per session.

## Key Changes

- **Removed legacy single GitManager**: Eliminated the `gitManager` dependency from `AppDeps` interface. The application no longer maintains a single shared git repository.

- **Implemented per-session git repos**: Each session now has its own git repository in `sessions/{sessionId}/`. The `createGitManager` factory function creates a `GitManager` instance for each session's directory.

- **Session-scoped git operations**: Modified `getActiveGitManager()` to require an active session and throw an error if git operations are attempted without one. This ensures all git operations target the correct session directory.

- **Deferred git identity checks**: Moved git identity validation from connection time to session activation time. When a session is activated via `get_chat_history`, the app now checks if that session's git repo has a configured identity and prompts the user if needed.

- **Updated all integration tests**: Modified 20+ test files to:
  - Create session directories with their own git repos in `beforeEach`
  - Track sessions with `SessionManager` before starting the app
  - Activate sessions by sending `get_chat_history` before performing git operations
  - Use session-specific directories for file operations and git verification

- **Improved TestClient timeout handling**: Fixed a race condition in `TestClient.receive()` where timed-out waiters could still consume future messages. Now properly removes stale waiters on timeout.

## Notable Implementation Details

- Session activation now triggers both file watcher restart and git identity check via the `activateSession()` function
- The `checkGitIdentity()` function gracefully handles missing session directories (identity check deferred until directory exists)
- Git operations that require an active session now fail with a clear error message instead of silently falling back to a non-existent root repo
- Session directories are created with `{ recursive: true }` to ensure parent directories exist

body:
## Summary

- Add environment configuration files (`.env.development`, `.env.production`) to support
  separate API URLs for the EC2 backend and the AWS API Gateway ML classification endpoint.
- Introduce a new **Camera Capture** page (`/camera`) with live device preview, snapshot
  capture, and ML classification via a dedicated classify API module that targets the
  Lambda endpoint independently from the CRUD API.
- Enhance the **Add Item** page with a side-by-side image source picker ("Upload Image"
  and "Connect Device / Camera") and support for pre-filled fields when navigating from
  the camera classification flow.
- Add "Camera" to the sidebar navigation.

## Motivation

The frontend needs to support an RGBD or phone camera for AI-powered item recognition.
This PR wires the full user journey: connect a device, preview the live feed, capture a
frame, send it to the ML classification Lambda (with graceful fallback while the backend
is still being deployed), review the result, and add the classified item to inventory
with pre-populated fields.

## Key changes

- **`frontend/.env.development`** / **`.env.production`** — `VITE_API_URL` for EC2 backend,
  `VITE_CLASSIFY_URL` for API Gateway + Lambda (placeholder until deployed)
- **`frontend/src/api/classify.js`** — separate axios instance targeting the classify
  endpoint so the ML Lambda can live at a different origin than the CRUD API
- **`frontend/src/pages/CameraCapturePage.jsx`** — device enumeration, getUserMedia live
  stream, canvas snapshot, classify call with mock fallback, "Add to Inventory" navigation
- **`frontend/src/App.jsx`** — `/camera` route
- **`frontend/src/components/Layout.jsx`** — Camera sidebar nav item
- **`frontend/src/pages/AddItemPage.jsx`** — two-option image source grid, prefill from
  camera navigation state

## How to test

- [ ] `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev`

      appear side-by-side

- [ ] Click "Capture Snapshot" — verify frozen frame appears

author: mnemosyn1154
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces significant performance optimizations to the backtesting engine and implements a proper trade execution callback system for strategy state management. Additionally, it includes security and reliability improvements across multiple modules.

## Key Changes

### Backtesting Engine Performance Optimization
- **Price lookup caching**: Pre-build `_price_lookup` dictionary (`{code: {date_str: close}}`) at engine startup to eliminate repeated `pd.to_datetime()` conversions during daily simulation loops
- **Price series caching**: Introduce `_price_series_cache` with sorted date-price tuples for O(log n) bisect-based lookups in `_get_prices_until()`
- **Refactored `_get_day_prices()`**: Simplified to O(1) dictionary lookups instead of repeated DataFrame filtering
- **Optimized `_get_prices_until()`**: Use `bisect_right()` for efficient date-based slicing with fallback to legacy logic for cache misses

### Dual Momentum Strategy - Trade Execution Callback
- **New `on_trade_executed()` method**: Implements callback pattern to update `current_allocation` only when trades are successfully executed
- **Metadata tracking**: Add `target_allocation` to signal metadata to distinguish intended vs. actual allocation state
- **Improved logging**: Clarify the difference between rebalancing signals and confirmed allocations

### Security & Reliability Improvements
- **Hash algorithm upgrade**: Replace MD5 with SHA256 for app key hashing in broker token caching (`src/core/broker.py`)
- **Environment loading guard**: Add `_env_loaded` flag to prevent duplicate `.env` loading across multiple calls
- **Async event loop handling**: Improve `notifier.py` to properly handle both running and non-running event loops using `asyncio.get_running_loop()` with proper exception handling

## Implementation Details
- Price caching is built once at `run()` initialization, reducing O(n) operations per day to O(1) lookups
- The callback system ensures strategy state remains consistent with actual executed trades, preventing divergence between intended and realized allocations
- Bisect-based slicing maintains O(log n) complexity for historical price queries while preserving look-ahead bias prevention

@a100_mig_env.task
async def hello_a100_partition() -> str:
    import asyncio
    import os

    visible = os.environ.get("NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "none")
    print(f"Hello from A100 80G MIG partition (1g.10gb)! NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES={visible}")

    total_seconds = 10 * 60
    interval = 60
    for elapsed in range(0, total_seconds, interval):
        remaining = (total_seconds - elapsed) // 60
        print(f"Running... {elapsed // 60} min elapsed, {remaining} min remaining")
        await asyncio.sleep(interval)

    msg = "Done! Ran for 10 minutes on A100 80G partition (1g.10gb)."
    print(msg)
    return msg

body:
## Description

Generated grids now include automatic row click navigation to edit pages. When `rowActionProp` is enabled, parent components can provide custom `onRowClick` handlers.

**Implementation:**

- **Default behavior**: Grids without `rowActionProp` automatically navigate to edit page via `stackSwitchApi.activatePage("edit", params.row.id)`
- **Custom behavior**: Grids with `rowActionProp` accept optional `onRowClick?: (params: GridRowParams) => void` prop
- **Opt-out**: Both modes respect `disableRowClick: true` config option

**Example with forwardRowAction:**

```tsx
// Generated grid accepts onRowClick prop
<ProductsGrid
  onRowClick={(params) => stackSwitchApi.activatePage("preview", params.row.id)}
  rowAction={(params) => <PreviewButton {...params} />}
/>
```

**Config:**
```typescript
export default defineConfig<GQLManufacturer>({
    type: "grid",
    gqlType: "Manufacturer",
    disableRowClick: true,  // Optional: disable row clicks

});

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a detailed specification document for the SerialBox Fortran preprocessor (`pp_ser`), which processes `!$SER` directives embedded in Fortran source code and expands them into serialization API calls.

## Changes

- **Added `development/references/directives_specification.md`**: A comprehensive 1075-line specification document covering:
  - Overview of the two-pass preprocessing model and scope tracking mechanism
  - General syntax rules including directive prefix, case insensitivity, line continuation, and argument tokenization
  - Complete reference for all 15 directive types:
    - Control directives: `INIT`, `CLEANUP`, `MODE`, `OPTION`, `ON`, `OFF`
    - Data serialization: `DATA`, `ACCDATA`, `DATA_KBUFF`
    - Metadata: `SAVEPOINT`, `METAINFO`, `REGISTER`, `REGISTERTRACERS`
    - Utility: `ZERO`, `TRACER`, `VERBATIM`
  - Detailed syntax, argument grammar, and generated code examples for each directive
  - Keyword abbreviations summary table
  - Automatic `USE` statement generation rules for both serialization and utility modules
  - Preprocessor configuration options and their effects
  - Error conditions and diagnostic messages
  - Complete EBNF-like grammar specification
  - Full worked example showing input directives and corresponding generated Fortran code

## Notable Details

- Documents the computed field detection mechanism (fields containing `*`, `+`, `-`, `/`, or `merge` are write-only)
- Specifies dimension shortcut codes for field registration (e.g., `IJK`, `IK1`) with their expansions
- Covers tracer specification grammar including name-based, index-based, and range-based access patterns
- Explains `#ifdef`/`#endif` guard generation and grouping behavior
- Documents special handling for `INTENT(IN)` removal when serialization is active
- Includes OpenACC integration via `ACCDATA` directive with conditional update directives

This specification serves as a reference for understanding and maintaining the preprocessor implementation.

### Motivation

body:
This pull request refactors how configuration and shared resources are managed and accessed across the codebase. The main change is the introduction of a singleton `Config` object (`config`) that centralizes configuration logic, replacing standalone functions and global variables. Additionally, a shared `console` instance is now used throughout the project for consistent Rich output. Several imports and usages have been updated to use these new shared objects.

**Configuration management refactor:**

* Introduced a singleton `Config` class in `soloquest/config.py` to centralize configuration, replacing individual functions like `get_adventures_dir`, `set_adventures_dir`, `saves_dir`, `sessions_dir`, and `journal_dir`. All configuration access now goes through the `config` object.
* Updated command-line argument handling in `soloquest/main.py` to use `config.set_adventures_dir()` instead of the old setter function.
* Changed all usages of configuration accessors in modules such as `soloquest/commands/character.py`, `soloquest/journal/exporter.py`, and `soloquest/state/save.py` to use the new `config` object. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b5e96fd376b7f6b9f182aeef1fe4e06886d0898b13caf321d2c3ea4ab9547fa9L98-R100) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6dabdbd2db63d4fac28876fbdcdb8a299800179cd2ce3d83b6802e7e83624dbL12-R23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c3e6b4f5861b8aa8d14f17b8927ec941707dd6bfa35ae31d00e332da07b0648bL9-R9) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c3e6b4f5861b8aa8d14f17b8927ec941707dd6bfa35ae31d00e332da07b0648bL18-R18)

**Shared console instance for Rich output:**

* Added a shared `console` instance in `soloquest/ui/console.py` and re-exported it from `soloquest/ui/__init__.py` for consistent Rich output across the project. author: copilot
body:
`amg_setup` is slow partly because it builds restriction maps needed only for partial resetup. `amg_resetup!` only supports partial resetup (recompute Galerkin products/smoothers). This adds control over both behaviors and eliminates code duplication between setup and full resetup.

### API changes

- **`amg_setup`**: new `allow_partial_resetup::Bool=true` kwarg. When `false`, skips `RestrictionMap` construction for faster setup.
- **`amg_resetup!`**: new `partial::Bool=true` kwarg. When `false`, re-coarsens from scratch reusing workspace arrays. Also accepts `allow_partial_resetup` to control map construction for subsequent resetups.

```julia
# Fast setup, no partial resetup support
h = amg_setup(A, config; allow_partial_resetup=false)

# Full re-coarsening resetup (works regardless of allow_partial_resetup)
amg_resetup!(h, A_new, config; partial=false)

# Restore partial resetup capability via full resetup
amg_resetup!(h, A_new, config; partial=false, allow_partial_resetup=true)
amg_resetup!(h, A_new2, config; partial=true)  # now works
```

### Internal refactoring

- Extracted `_build_levels!` and `_build_coarse_solver` from `amg_setup` — shared by both `amg_setup` and `amg_resetup!(partial=false)`
- `_build_levels!` reuses workspace vectors (`r`, `xc`, `bc`) from old levels when sizes match via `_reuse_or_allocate_vector`
- `AMGLevel.R_map` type widened to `Union{Nothing, RestrictionMap}`
- `compute_coarse_sparsity` gains `build_restriction_map::Bool=true` to skip Phase 3 (triple grouping)
- All 6 GPU/format extensions updated to forward new kwargs

## Changes

The app aggregates forecasts from 4 weather models (ICON, GFS, AROME, GEM). Previously:

```javascript
// Hourly forecast - was using average
wind: Math.round(getAvg('windspeed_10m')),

// Daily forecast - correctly using max
wind: Math.round(Math.max(
  d.windspeed_10m_max_icon_seamless?.[i] || 0,
  d.windspeed_10m_max_gfs_seamless?.[i] || 0,
  d.windspeed_10m_max_arome_seamless?.[i] || 0,
  d.windspeed_10m_max_gem_seamless?.[i] || 0
)),
```

Now hourly uses `getMax()` which internally performs the same max operation as daily forecasts.

author: lee-jaejin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12873. When the iMessage bridge delivers the bot’s own messages back as inbound with `is_from_me` null or missing, the bot treated them as user messages and produced echo/loops. This PR fixes that.

**Cause:** Previously we (1) dropped “from me” only when `is_from_me` was truthy, and (2) used a 5-second TTL text cache to suppress “recently sent bot message” echoes. The bridge sometimes sends bot messages with `is_from_me: null`, and when LLM inference exceeds 5 seconds the TTL expires so echoes get through — both mechanisms failed in those cases.

**What this branch does:**  
Echo/duplicate handling now uses **content-hash-based detection** and **`is_from_me` early exit** together.

- **Hash-based echo detection:** When the bot sends a message we store `SHA-256(scope + text)`. On inbound, if the same hash exists we treat it as a bot echo and drop it. No TTL; a FIFO cap of 200 entries and one-shot removal on match reduce false positives and bound memory.
- **`is_from_me` early exit:** If the bridge reports `is_from_me: true`, we drop immediately so the same user message is not processed twice.
- **Shared scope:** `echo-scope.ts` ensures delivery and inbound use the same scope key so hashes align.

So: bridge-reported “from me” → early exit; when `is_from_me` is null/missing, bot echoes are caught by hash matching.

**Code changes:**  
`SentMessageCache` is extracted into its own module and now stores/checks hashes with a bounded FIFO; `monitor-provider` uses it. In `inbound-processing` we early-return when `is_from_me` is set, then rely on the hash-based echo cache for everything else. On delivery we build scope via shared `buildIMessageEchoScope` and only store the hash in the cache. Review follow-ups: removed the stale 5-second TTL comment and the redundant pre-chunk `remember()` call.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `SentMessageCache` (hash storage, echo match, FIFO eviction, one-shot removal)
- [x] Unit tests for `echo-scope` (DM/group scope identical between delivery and inbound)
- [x] `deliverReplies`-related tests
- [ ] Manual: verify no echo loop with slow inference (e.g. local Ollama >5s)

This pull request adds a new implementation for generating the sitemap at `sitemap.xml.tsx`. The new code dynamically collects all static and post routes, filters out unwanted files and dynamic routes, and generates a compliant XML sitemap response with appropriate metadata.

**Sitemap generation improvements:**

* Added logic to dynamically import and filter all static route files, excluding API, test, and special files, to build the list of sitemap routes (`getRoutes`).
* Implemented `getPostRoutes` to fetch post slugs from the storage bucket and generate corresponding `/posts/{slug}` routes for the sitemap.
* Built a utility to safely escape XML characters in URLs and generate the sitemap XML with standard metadata such as `lastmod`, `changefreq`, and `priority`.
* Registered a new route handler that responds with the generated sitemap XML, sets the correct content type, and applies caching headers.

author: e-l-t
body:
**Ce que fait la PR**
Actuellement dans les vignettes de la galerie de pjs, pour les pdfs, on affiche la grande version de l'image et non la petite. C'est corrigé dans le 1er commit. Et dans le 2e, c'est du renommage autour des notions de variant et de représentation.

**Le contexte**
- Quand un usager uploade une image dans un dossier, cela crée 2 blobs : 
  - Le blob de l'image dont l'attachment a un record_type: "champ" 
  - Le blob de la miniature de l'image dont l'attachment a un record_type: "ActiveStorage::VariantRecord"

- Quand un usager uploade un pdf dans un dossier, cela crée 3 blobs : 
  - le blob du pdf, dont l'attachment a un record_type: "champ"
  - le blob de l'image de preview dont l'attachment a un record_type: "ActiveStorage::Blob"
  - le blob de l'image miniature de la preview dont l'attachment a un record_type: "ActiveStorage::VariantRecord"

Il y avait une confusion autour de la notion de représentation. Dans Active Storage une représentation englobe les deux façons de générer une image à partir d'un blob : un variant à partir d'une image, ou une preview à partir d'un pdf ou d'une vidéo. Et on confondait la preview de la pdf avec la miniature de la preview de pdf

**Résumé**
Dans notre cas, une représentation peut être :
- une miniature d'image (variant)
- une prévisualisation de pdf (preview_image)
- une miniature de prévisualisation de pdf (variant)

author: cylosia
body:
## Summary

This PR documents the results of a comprehensive security audit covering the frontend (`apps/web/`), control plane API (`control-plane/`), and shared packages (`packages/config/`, `packages/kernel/`, `packages/monitoring/`). The audit identified **2 critical P0 vulnerabilities** requiring immediate remediation, **22 high-severity P1 findings**, and additional medium and low-priority issues.

## Key Findings

### Critical (P0) — Immediate Action Required
- **Frontend Authentication Bypass**: `ClerkProvider` is missing from `_app.tsx`, and the middleware unconditionally passes requests without a `__session` cookie, allowing unauthenticated access to all protected routes.
- **Auth Rate-Limit Broken in Kubernetes**: The `authRateLimit` middleware uses `req.ip` without `trustProxy` enabled, causing all clients to share a single rate-limit bucket in K8s deployments. This enables both DoS attacks and trivial brute-force attacks.

### High (P1) — Remediate This Sprint
Notable findings include:
- `BASE_SECURITY_HEADERS` is runtime-mutable (no `Object.freeze()` or `as const`)
- CORS origin sourced from `NEXT_PUBLIC_` client-side environment variable
- SSRF vulnerability in `createExternalApiHealthCheck` (both kernel and monitoring implementations)
- Full `HealthReport` and process metadata exposed on unauthenticated monitoring endpoints
- Missing `Cache-Control: no-store` in base security headers
- IDOR on domain pages (UUID validated but ownership not checked)
- Swagger UI served unconditionally in production
- Stack traces leaked in non-production error responses
- Open redirect vulnerability via protocol-relative paths
- Multiple missing security header validations and test coverage gaps

### Medium (P2) — Backlog
- CSP nonce injection refuted via cross-validation (reclassified from P0 to P2 defense-in-depth concern)
- Wildcard `connect-src` in CSP policy
- Missing test coverage for header immutability and CSP directives
- Rate-limit configuration not validated at startup

### Low (P3) — Technical Debt
- Unschematized health check metadata
- Inconsistent error status codes
- Duplicated `healthPath` constant
- Missing `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on external links

## Remediation Priority

The report includes a prioritized remediation order with effort estimates. The two P0 vulnerabilities should be addressed before the next production deployment. All 22 P1 findings should be remediated within the current sprint.

## Files Affected

Changes required across:
- `apps/web/pages/_app.tsx`, `middleware.ts`, `pages/domains/[domainId].tsx`, `components/DomainTabs.tsx`
- `control-plane/api/http.ts`
- `packages/config/headers.ts`
- `packages/kernel/health-check.ts`
- `packages/monitoring/health-checks.ts`, `init.ts`
- Test suite (new test coverage)

## Cross-Validation

One previously-reported P0 finding (CSP nonce injection via `buildWebAppCsp`) was **refuted** by adversarial cross-validation: the nonce is always cryptographically generated Base64, making injection structurally impossible in the current codebase.

> **Overview**
> **Dynamic config expansion:** Adds `class_manager_dynamic_config` and `state_sync_dynamic_config` to `NodeDynamicConfig`, exposes new `ConfigManager` RPCs (`GetClassManagerDynamicConfig`, `GetStateSyncDynamicConfig`), and wires `apollo_node` to pass a `ConfigManager` client into the class manager and state sync so they can refresh dynamic config at runtime.
> 
> **Config & storage changes:** Refactors class manager config into `static_config`/`dynamic_config`, adds storage-reader-server static+dynamic config to class storage, and updates deployment JSON/config schema accordingly. Central sync replaces the `store_sierras_and_casms` boolean with `store_sierras_and_casms_block_threshold`, and now propagates `block_number` with compiled-class events so storage decisions can be made per block.
> 
> **Batcher/commitment + observability:** `Batcher::get_block_hash` now flushes pending commitment results to storage before reading, adds related tests and log improvements, and lowers commitment-manager/state-committer logs to `debug`. Committer metrics are converted from histograms to cumulative counters (adding `blocks_committed`), and Grafana/dashboard panels are updated to compute per-block averages via `increase(...)` ratios; pod disk panels now group by PVC. Also enables `cairo_native` as a feature in `apollo_gateway` and propagates it via `apollo_node`/integration tests, and adds additional staking/consensus logging and dependency wiring.
>

author: willeastbury
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/WillEastbury/BareMetalWeb/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/WillEastbury/BareMetalWeb/security/code-scanning/1)

To fix the problem, explicitly add a `permissions` block that grants the least privileges required for this workflow. Since the workflow only checks out code and then builds/tests/deploys using Azure credentials from secrets, it only needs read access to repository contents. It does not need to write to the repo, manage pull requests, or access other scopes.

The best minimal fix is to add a top-level `permissions` block with `contents: read` right after the `name:` (or before/after `on:`) so it applies to all jobs. Concretely, in `.github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml`, between line 1 (`name: Deploy to Production`) and line 3 (`on:`), insert:

```yml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

No additional methods, imports, or definitions are required; this is purely a YAML configuration change to the workflow.

author: mb116
body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for **Filament v5** and **Livewire v4**.

### Changes

#### \composer.json\
- Bumped \ ilament/filament\ dependency from \^4.0\ to \^5.0\
- Added \^13.0\ to \illuminate/contracts\ version constraint
- Removed \orchestra/testbench ^7.0\ (incompatible with Filament v5 / Laravel 11+)
- Dropped \pestphp/pest-plugin-livewire ^2.0\ (Livewire v4 requires \^3.0\)

#### Event listeners: \\->listeners\ → \#[On]\ attributes
Livewire v4 deprecates the \\->listeners\ array in favor of the \#[On]\ PHP attribute. The old approach still works but is not recommended.

- **\UsesResourceLock\**: removed \ ootUsesResourceLock()\ boot method, added \#[On('resourceLockObserver::init')]\, \#[On('resourceLockObserver::unload')]\ and \#[On('resourceLockObserver::unlock')]\ attributes to the corresponding handler methods
- **\UsesSimpleResourceLock\**: removed \ ootUsesSimpleResourceLock()\ boot method, added \#[On('resourceLockObserver::unload')]\ and \#[On('resourceLockObserver::unlock')]\ attributes
- **\UsesLocks\**: added \#[On('resourceLockObserver::renewLock')]\ attribute to \enewLock()\

#### Blade component rendering
Livewire v4 requires component tags to be properly closed. Replaced the deprecated \@livewire()\ Blade directive with a self-closing component tag:

\\\php
// Before
Blade::render('@livewire(\'resource-lock-observer\')')

// After
Blade::render('<livewire:resource-lock-observer />')
\\\

### Compatibility

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| PHP | ^8.2 |
| Laravel | ^11.28 |
| Filament | ^5.0 |
| Livewire | ^4.0 (pulled in by Filament v5) |

author: dimagious
body:
## Summary
Refactored ExplainIt! from a backend-dependent architecture to direct AI provider API calls. Users can now select from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or Groq and provide their own API keys, which are stored locally for security.

## Key Changes

### Architecture
- **Removed backend dependency**: Eliminated all references to `dy-budget-helper.ru` backend server
- **Direct provider APIs**: Background service worker now calls OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Groq APIs directly using user-provided API keys
- **Provider-agnostic prompt system**: Moved prompt templates from backend to `config.js` and `background.js`

### Settings & Storage
- **Dual storage strategy**: 
  - Preferences (language, tone) → `chrome.storage.sync` (cross-device)
  - Provider + API keys → `chrome.storage.local` (device-only, security)
- **Draft key management**: Unsaved API key edits tracked in `draftApiKeys` map; persisted only on explicit save
- **Provider switching**: Users can switch between providers mid-session without losing typed keys

### UI/UX
- **Provider selection cards**: Radio button grid with provider name, model label, and visual feedback
- **API key input**: Password field with show/hide toggle and provider-specific placeholder text
- **Settings badge**: Result screen displays active provider, language, and tone
- **Error handling**: Distinguishes auth errors (show "Open Settings") from transient errors (show "Retry")

### API Implementation
- **OpenAI-compatible callers**: Unified handler for OpenAI and Groq (both use `Authorization: Bearer` header)
- **Provider-specific handlers**: Separate implementations for Anthropic (`x-api-key` header) and Gemini (key in URL query param)
- **Retry logic**: Retries on 5xx errors; fails immediately on 401/403 auth errors to avoid quota waste
- **Timeout & resilience**: 30s timeout with exponential backoff; graceful error messages

### Testing
- **Unit tests added**: `config.test.js`, `popup.test.js`, `background.test.js`
- **Real bug coverage**: Tests verify correct API header formats, response parsing, storage routing, and settings validation
- **No external dependencies**: Tests use Jest with mocked `chrome` APIs and `fetch`

### Security
- **API keys never synced**: Keys stored in `chrome.storage.local` only, never in `chrome.storage.sync`
- **Scoped host permissions**: Manifest updated to allow only specific provider domains (not `<all_urls>`)
- **Client-side validation**: Settings validated before save; invalid providers/languages rejected

## Implementation Details
- Prompt templates now inline in `background.js` and `config.js` (no backend calls)
- `PROVIDER_META` object in `popup.js` mirrors `PROVIDERS` in `config.js` for UI consistency
- Error detection uses `err.status` code to distinguish auth (4xx) from server (5xx) errors
- Settings form uses `onProviderSwitch()` to persist current key before switching providers

body:
Implements executable compilation for the Photobooth application using PyInstaller, enabling distribution without Python installation.

## Build Configuration

- **photobooth.spec**: PyInstaller spec file configured for PyQt6/OpenCV with hidden imports for Windows modules (win32print, pywin32), bundled assets/config/src directories, GUI mode (no console)
- **requirements-build.txt**: Isolated build dependencies from runtime requirements
- **Platform-aware executable detection** in build.py for cross-platform compatibility

## Build Automation

- **build.py**: Validates PyInstaller availability, cleans artifacts, builds executable, verifies output
- **build.bat/build.sh**: One-click compilation for Windows and Unix systems

## Documentation

- **docs/BUILD.md**: Build instructions, troubleshooting, customization options, distribution guide
- **DISTRIBUTION_README.md**: End-user setup guide bundled with compiled application

## Usage

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt requirements-build.txt

# Build executable
python build.py
# Output: dist/Photobooth/Photobooth.exe (+ dependencies)
```

Windows users can double-click `build.bat` for automated compilation. The resulting `dist/Photobooth/` directory is self-contained and distributable.

body:
PR #40 was deployed but changes invisible to users due to aggressive browser caching of `main.js`. Without cache invalidation, browsers serve stale JavaScript indefinitely despite server-side updates.

## Changes

- **Added version query parameters** to CSS and JS references in `index.html`
  ```html
  <!-- Before -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <script src="main.js" defer></script>
  
  <!-- After -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css?v=2.0">
  <script src="main.js?v=2.0" defer></script>
  ```

- **Created user documentation** explaining the caching issue and browser refresh instructions

## Impact

Gallery now displays correctly with reorganized images from PR #40. Future updates require incrementing version parameter (`?v=2.1`, `?v=3.0`, etc.) to force cache invalidation.

![Gallery displaying with all color categories](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7641d51-355f-469a-9778-e421387a2113)

Users must hard refresh (`Ctrl+Shift+R` / `Cmd+Shift+R`) once to clear existing cache.

author: justinhartfield
body:
## What

Adds OpenClaw support to the installer so `curl | bash` works for OpenClaw users.

## Changes

- **`--openclaw` flag** — explicitly install as an OpenClaw skill
- **Auto-detection** — if `~/.openclaw` exists and `~/.claude` does not, automatically installs for OpenClaw
- **OpenClaw skill file** — creates `~/.openclaw/skills/peon-ping/SKILL.md` with usage docs
- **Skips settings.json** — OpenClaw doesn't use Claude Code's hook registration
- **Uses existing adapter** — leverages `adapters/openclaw.sh` that already maps OpenClaw events to peon-ping sounds

## Usage

```bash
# Explicit
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --openclaw

# Auto-detected (when ~/.openclaw exists, ~/.claude doesn't)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.sh | bash
```

## Notes

- Sound packs, adapters, shell aliases, and trainer all install normally
- The adapter at `adapters/openclaw.sh` was already in the repo — this PR just makes the installer aware of it
- No changes to existing Claude Code / Cursor install paths

### Motivation
- Provide an actionable, end-to-end engineering plan to meet strict, measurable UX/performance targets for a local/NAS comic reader and eliminate common slow-paths (no thumbnails, large decodes, blocking loads). 
- Capture concrete architecture choices, API surface, data model, performance techniques, and phased milestones so implementation can be executed with performance-first tradeoffs.

### Description
- Add `EXECUTABLE_PLAN.md` containing A) architecture decision, B) key techniques checklist (thumbnailing, caching, virtualization, prefetch, concurrency limits, decode/memory control), C) minimal API list, D) data model outline, E) phased milestones, F) performance validation plan, and G) risks/tradeoffs plus a 2-week backlog. 
- Recommend frontend stack `SvelteKit + Vite + TypeScript + Service Worker` and backend `Go + SQLite` with a thumbnail cache directory and bounded background worker pools for scan/thumbnail tasks. 
- Provide concrete route definitions and payload outlines for library, manga, chapters, pages, image endpoints, and scan tasks, plus DB table/index recommendations sized for thousands of manga. 
- Include measurable exit criteria and instrumentation guidance (FCP/LCP/first page render, TTFB, scroll FPS) and operations guidance for NAS and cache management.

- Ran `wc -l EXECUTABLE_PLAN.md` to verify file length, which returned `379` lines.

# Pull Request (PR)

## Pull Request Title
`fix: share CryptoSoft build/copy target for GUI and Console`

---

## Description
This PR centralizes `CryptoSoft.exe` build/copy logic so both GUI and Console outputs are handled consistently.

### What changed
- Added shared MSBuild target in `Directory.Build.targets` to:
  - build `src/CryptoSoft/CryptoSoft.csproj`
  - copy `CryptoSoft.exe` into `$(OutputPath)\Resources`
- Enabled the shared target in:
  - `src/GUI/GUI.csproj` (`CopyCryptoSoftToResources=true`)
  - `src/Console/Console.csproj` (`CopyCryptoSoftToResources=true`)
- Removed old per-project/hardcoded copy logic:
  - removed GUI local target
  - removed Console local target
  - removed hardcoded Debug path copy from `src/Application/Application.csproj`

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
# Pull Request Summary: Harden Image (PR #158)

## Overview
This PR hardens the Docker image and refactors presentation/versioning concerns. Major themes: multi-stage distroless containerization with a pruned, isolated install prefix; removal of the emoji dependency in favor of a centralized icons module with selectable themes; single-source versioning; pinned runtime dependencies; added distroless-safe healthcheck and tests; and assorted test and example updates to align with container usage.

## Key Changes

- Docker / Containerization
  - Full Dockerfile rewrite to a multi-stage build:
    - Builder: python:3.11-slim (with build deps and optional Rust toolchain support).
    - Runtime: distroless python3-debian12:nonroot plus a runtime-debug target with shell/tools for troubleshooting.
  - Installs into an isolated /install prefix in builder, prunes packaging artifacts, strips shared objects and pyc files, and copies only runtime files into /usr/local in final image.
  - Exposes fine-grained build-time args and environment variables to control pip behavior, wheel selection, bytecode writing, and optional native builds.
  - Uses numeric nonroot UID/GID 65532:65532 in final image, sets PYTHONPATH and MCP_FUZZER_IN_DOCKER environment flags.
  - Replaces prior ENTRYPOINT/HEALTHCHECK forms with:
    - ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/python3", "-m", "mcp_fuzzer"]
    - HEALTHCHECK that invokes mcp_fuzzer.healthcheck
    - CMD defaults to ["--help"]
  - Adds docker/requirements.runtime.txt with pinned runtime deps and documentation updates (QUICKSTART, README) describing debug target, healthcheck invocation, and native-build guidance.
  - Adds a container smoke test script tests/e2e/test_healthcheck_container.sh to run the healthcheck inside the image.

- Versioning
  - Introduces mcp_fuzzer/version.py exposing VERSION = "0.2.9".
  - mcp_fuzzer/__init__.py imports VERSION as __version__ and exposes it via __all__.
  - pyproject.toml updated to use a dynamic version attribute (setuptools dynamic config).

- Presentation / Dependencies
  - Removes the emoji dependency (pyproject and requirements.txt).
  - Adds mcp_fuzzer/utils/icons.py exposing theme-backed constants (CHECK, CROSS, ALERT, SHIELD, BLOCKED, UNLOCKED, TARGET, ROCKET, STATS) and current_theme() with a default ascii theme.
  - Replaces emoji usage with icon constants across multiple modules and formatters:
    - mcp_fuzzer/cli/validators.py
    - mcp_fuzzer/client/main.py
    - mcp_fuzzer/reports/formatters/markdown_fmt.py
    - mcp_fuzzer/safety_system/blocking/command_blocker.py
    - mcp_fuzzer/safety_system/blocking/shims/default_shim.py
    - mcp_fuzzer/safety_system/safety.py

- Healthcheck & Testing
  - Adds mcp_fuzzer/healthcheck.py with run_healthcheck(verbose: bool) -> int and main(argv) entrypoint; verifies version import and presence of schemas; supports JSON verbose output.
  - Adds unit and e2e tests:
    - tests/unit/test_healthcheck.py (unit tests for healthcheck)
    - tests/unit/cli/test_cli.py verifies --version behavior
    - tests/unit/reports/test_formatters_extra.py and safety_system tests updated to expect new icon outputs
    - tests/e2e/test_healthcheck_container.sh for running healthcheck inside built image
  - Adds tests/README.md note for running the container smoke test.

- Examples & Minor API Surface Changes
  - examples/test_server.py updated to use environment-driven binding and token handling (BIND_HOST, BIND_PORT, REQUIRED_TOKEN, ALLOWED_ORIGIN).
  - Several method signatures reformatted (multiline) in protocol handler; presentation-only changes elsewhere.
  - ENTRYPOINT/HEALTHCHECK/USER declarations in the Dockerfile are public-facing runtime contract changes (numeric USER, Python module-based entrypoint and healthcheck).

## Design Analysis

- Patterns Used / Design Shifts
  - Multi-stage Build pattern: clear builder/runtime separation, isolated install prefix, deterministic artifact selection.
  - Single Responsibility / Module Extraction: version and icon concerns moved to dedicated modules (mcp_fuzzer/version.py, mcp_fuzzer/utils/icons.py).
  - Dependency Abstraction: icons module abstracts presentation tokens away from a third-party library, enabling theming.
  - Defensive Packaging: pinned runtime deps + pruning reduce attack surface and improve reproducibility.

- SOLID Assessment
  - Single Responsibility Principle (SRP): improved — versioning and icon presentation responsibilities are isolated into single-purpose modules.
  - Open/Closed Principle (OCP): improved — icons module supports theme extension without modifying consumers; packaging behavior is controlled via build args.
  - Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP): not materially impacted — replacements are backward-compatible string constants where emojis were used.
  - Interface Segregation Principle (ISP): acceptable — modules import only needed icon constants; CLI parser adds a version flag only.
  - Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP): partially improved — code now depends on an internal abstracted icons module rather than a third-party emoji library, lowering external coupling.

## Code & Design Smells, Risks, and Review Concerns

- Container/runtime risks
  - Distroless runtime removes shell and common utilities; any code or tests that assume a shell or /bin/sh will fail. Ensure healthcheck, entrypoint, and runtime invocations require no shell.
  - Pruning steps (removing .so, pyc, tests, pip artifacts) risk accidentally stripping needed C extensions or runtime metadata; verify C extension .so files and shared libs are preserved and wheel metadata needed at runtime is present.

- Build complexity
  - Optional Rust toolchain and native-build support increase builder image size and CI resource use. CI pipelines must accommodate these build-args or default to binary wheels. Document and exercise the native-build path in CI if required.

- API/Behavior surface
  - Public runtime contract changed: ENTRYPOINT now explicitly uses python3 -m mcp_fuzzer and HEALTHCHECK runs mcp_fuzzer.healthcheck; image USER changed to numeric 65532. Consumers relying on the previous entrypoint, shell access, or user mapping should be validated.
  - Versioning: dynamic setuptools configuration referencing mcp_fuzzer.version.VERSION must be validated in packaging and release automation to avoid mismatches during builds/releases.

- Tests & UX
  - Many tests adjusted for new icon text; ensure all emoji-dependent tests and any third-party integrations are updated. Theme selection via MCP_FUZZER_ICON_THEME may affect CI snapshot tests if different environments default differently—CI should set the theme explicitly when required.
  - Presentation choice: ASCII default may reduce visual clarity compared to emoji/unicode for some users; theming mitigates this but confirm defaults and docs align with expected UX.

- Minor smells
  - Some method signature reformatting (multiline) is stylistic; review for unintended linter/typing impacts.
  - Large Dockerfile with many build args increases surface for misconfiguration; consider consolidating common flags or documenting defaults clearly.

## Suggested Review Focus
- Verify the Dockerfile pruning preserves necessary runtime artifacts (C extensions, .so files, package metadata).
- Run the full test suite inside the distroless runtime (or at least exercise healthcheck and key runtime paths) to validate the no-shell constraint.
- Confirm CI build agents have resources and permissions for optional native builds or that binary-wheel-first approach is enforced by CI.
- Validate packaging workflow with dynamic versioning (setuptools dynamic) and update release automation if needed.
- Ensure all consumer-facing changes (ENTRYPOINT, HEALTHCHECK, USER) are communicated in docs and release notes.
- Ensure theme/environment defaults (MCP_FUZZER_ICON_THEME) are deterministic in CI to avoid flaky snapshot tests.

author: cylosia
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses multiple security and reliability issues across the codebase, including race conditions in queue management, input validation to prevent DoS attacks, cache poisoning vulnerabilities, and ID collision risks.

## Key Changes

### Email Provider & Retry Queue (P2 Fix)
- **Atomic queue operations**: Changed `queueForRetry()` to use Redis pipelines (`MULTI/EXEC`) for atomic `lpush` + `ltrim` operations, eliminating a race condition where concurrent writers could temporarily exceed the queue size cap
- **Unique message IDs**: Added random suffix to log provider message IDs (`log-${Date.now()}-${random}`) to prevent ID collisions under concurrent sends, which was breaking retry deduplication
- **Header length validation**: Added 2048-character limit to `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` header values to prevent mail-server parsing bugs and exceed-limit errors (RFC 5322 compliance)

### Fencing Token Validation (P1 Fix)
- **Input length limits**: Added 255-character maximum length validation for `resourceType` and `resourceId` parameters to prevent DoS via oversized query parameters that could OOM the PostgreSQL server
- **Whitespace handling**: Changed validation from falsy check to explicit `.trim()` check to reject whitespace-only strings that would pass the original check but create phantom fence-token rows

### Flag Service (P2 Fix)
- **Result set limiting**: Added `LIMIT 10000` to `getAll()` query to prevent OOM if the flags table grows unboundedly; includes TODO comment for future structured warning logging

### Cache Key Generation (P1 Fix)
- **Auth header safety**: Fixed potential undefined access in `generateCacheKey()` when processing header tuples — malformed headers with missing values could produce empty auth segments, causing cross-user cache poisoning

### Test Updates
- Updated Redis mocks in `fallback.test.ts` to reflect the new pipeline-based implementation, ensuring `multi()`, `lpush()`, `ltrim()`, and `exec()` are properly mocked and verified

### Code Cleanup
- Removed redundant `orgId` validation in `feedbackIngestJob.ts` (already validated by Zod schema)

## Implementation Details
- All fixes maintain backward compatibility while improving atomicity and safety
- DoS prevention limits are conservative (255 chars for DB params, 2048 for headers, 10k for flag rows) to avoid impacting legitimate use cases
- Cache poisoning fix uses defensive null-coalescing to handle malformed header tuples gracefully

body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive support for creating model elements and annotations in Revit, along with parameter value retrieval. It introduces 8 new command handlers and corresponding MCP server tools to enable programmatic creation of walls, floors, railings, dimensions, text notes, family instances, and groups, plus parameter value queries.

## Key Changes

### New Command Handlers (Core)
- **CreateWallHandler**: Creates straight walls between two points on a specified level with configurable height, type, and structural flag
- **CreateFloorHandler**: Creates floors from closed boundary polygons with support for floor type selection and structural designation
- **CreateRailingHandler**: Creates railings along multi-segment paths with type selection
- **CreateDimensionHandler**: Creates dimensions between 2+ elements with automatic reference extraction from geometry and optional dimension type specification
- **CreateTextNoteHandler**: Creates text note annotations in views with type selection
- **InsertFamilyInstanceByPointHandler**: Places component family instances (furniture, fixtures, doors, windows) at points on levels with type and structural options
- **InsertGroupHandler**: Inserts group instances at specified coordinates
- **GetParameterValueHandler**: Retrieves single parameter values from elements, checking both instance and type parameters with helpful error messages listing available parameters

### New MCP Server Tools
- **CreationTools**: Exposes `create_wall`, `create_text_note`, `create_railing`, and `create_dimension` tools with full parameter documentation
- **FamilyTools**: Exposes `insert_family_instance_by_point` and `insert_group` tools
- **ParameterTools**: Exposes `get_parameter_value` tool for efficient single-parameter queries

### Core Updates
- Extended `CommandNames` class with 8 new command constants
- Updated `App.cs` to register all new handlers in the command handler registry

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Unit Conversion**: All handlers consistently convert millimeters to Revit's internal feet units using `UnitUtils.ConvertToInternalUnits`
- **Geometry Reference Extraction**: CreateDimensionHandler includes recursive geometry traversal to extract usable references from elements, with fallback strategies for different geometry types
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive validation with helpful error messages that list available options (levels, types, families) when lookups fail
- **Transaction Management**: All creation operations properly wrap changes in transactions with rollback on failure
- **Type Flexibility**: Optional type parameters default to first available type when not specified, improving usability
- **Parameter Discovery**: GetParameterValueHandler lists available parameters when requested parameter is not found, aiding discoverability

author: rovinlr
body:
### Motivation
- En algunos casos la orden POS con tipo FE `electronic_ticket` quedaba pagada pero sin `account_move` listo al intentar firmar, por lo que no se enviaba el comprobante electrónico a Hacienda.
- `_trigger_fe_signature` podía recibir un `pos.order` y no redirigir al `account_move` relacionado, provocando que no se ejecutara el método de firmado adecuado.

### Description
- Se añade una redirección en `_trigger_fe_signature` para detectar cuando se pasa un `pos.order` y llamar al `account_move` asociado con `PosOrder._trigger_fe_signature(move.account_move.sudo())`.
- Se introduce el método `_ensure_ticket_invoice_and_sign` que valida que la orden sea `electronic_ticket`, comprueba el estado (`paid`, `done`, `invoiced`), genera la factura POS con `_generate_pos_order_invoice` si falta y dispara el firmado/envío sobre el `account_move`.
- Se reemplaza la llamada directa al firmado en `_process_order` por `self._ensure_ticket_invoice_and_sign(pos_order_record)` para garantizar la generación del `account_move` antes de firmar.
- Los cambios mantienen la compatibilidad con las distintas versiones de Odoo y con los métodos de firmado que expone `l10n_cr_einvoice`.

### Testing
- Se ejecutó `python3 -m py_compile pos_factura_electronica/models/pos_order.py` y la comprobación de sintaxis fue exitosa.
- No se añadieron tests unitarios automáticos adicionales en este cambio.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds `classNames` overrides to the `Calendar` component within `DateRangePicker` to style the dual-month calendar layout — removing the gap between months (`gap-0` instead of `gap-4`) and adding a left border separator between them. - The `classNames` prop uses an object spread in `Calendar` (`...classNames`), which **fully replaces** the default computed class strings rather than merging with them. This causes the `month` override to drop essential layout classes (`flex flex-col w-full gap-4`) and react-day-picker's own `defaultClassNames`, which may break month panel rendering. - The `months` override similarly drops `defaultClassNames.months` from react-day-picker, though the custom classes largely replicate the needed flex layout.

body:
### Purpose
This PR ensures that embargo, publish_schedule, and schedule_settings fields are preserved when duplicating content to a desk in the "Send and Duplicate" flow. This is implemented via a client-side configuration flag that only affects the Send and Duplicate action, leaving regular duplication flows unchanged.

### What has changed
- Modified `DuplicateService.create_async()` to conditionally preserve fields when the flag is set
- Added test scenario 

### Steps to test
1. Configure `sendAndDuplicate.preserveEmbargoAndSchedule: true` in superdesk.config.js like for STT
2. Create a story on any desk and add embargo and publishing schedule dates
3. Save the story
4. Click the "Send and Duplicate" button (sends to the configured target desk, e.g., Deski)
5. Verify the duplicated story in the target desk has the same:
   - Embargo date
   - Publishing schedule date
   - Schedule settings (timezone)
6. Verify the original story retains its embargo and schedule information
7. Test regular "Duplicate To" flow - fields should NOT be preserved

Note: This PR is related to this [PR in superdesk-stt](https://github.com/superdesk/superdesk-stt/pull/710), and [PR in superdesk-client-core](https://github.com/superdesk/superdesk-client-core/pull/5079)

author: copilot
body:
User model extended `Model` instead of `Authenticatable`, causing type mismatch during login validation: `Argument #1 ($user) must be of type Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable, App\Models\User given`.

## Changes

- Changed base class from `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model` to `Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User`
- Added `Notifiable` trait
- Added `$hidden` property for `password` and `remember_token`
- Added `password` cast to `hashed` for Laravel 12 compatibility

```php
// Before
class User extends Model
{
    use HasFactory;
    
    protected $casts = [
        'role' => Role::class,
        'is_active' => 'boolean',
    ];
}

// After
class User extends Authenticatable
{
    use HasFactory, Notifiable;
    
    protected $hidden = [
        'password',
        'remember_token',
    ];
    
    protected $casts = [
        'role' => Role::class,
        'is_active' => 'boolean',
        'password' => 'hashed',
    ];
}
```

## Summary

## Summary
Translates the comprehensive Feature_Spec.md (3,795 lines, 153 subsections) into a structured features.json file following Anthropic's guidelines for long-running agent testing.

- **features.json** (1,616 lines): 151 testable features with category, description, steps, and passes fields

- **functional**: 92 features (60.9%) - Timer operations, CRUD, workflows

{

author: makramkd
body:
This PR updates the standalone deployment of the committee verifier to use the `bootstrap` library. As such:

* Jobs get proposed by JD rather than mounted as a config file
* Keys get generated by the bootstrap process rather than in the devenv environment setup

Library-level changes:
* Add an "info server" to the bootstrap library; the idea behind this is to expose a health endpoint for docker and to get the public keys for the keys that were created as part of the bootstrap sequence.
* Add a `pgstore` wrapper that properly handles `sql.ErrNoRows`. Currently, we can't call `LoadKeystore` with an empty keystore. This seems to be a bug in the keystore library, but we handle it gracefully here using a wrapper so that we're not blocked and can investigate this issue afterwards with the keystore maintainers.
* Change JD connect logic in the lifecycle manager to be async instead of sync so that devenv startup is smoother, since JD registration can only happen after we get the CSA keys from the info server, which only starts up properly after the entire bootstrap startup sequence is finished.
* Add a `verifier.MessageSigner` implementation that uses the keystore.

Driver program (e.g. main.go) changes:
* Changes the committee verifier's `main.go` to use the `bootstrap.Run` method; startup related code has been moved to `servicefactory.go`

Devenv-level changes:
* Changes in `committeeVerifier.go` to support a bootstrapped committee verifier. As such, we create the bootstrap database in the postgres container that is started, we expose the info server port, and we fetch the CSA and signing keys from the info server prior to returning.
* Changed startup sequence to start the standalone verifiers earlier, since they're bootstrapped. They're then registered w/ JD. 
* Key generation logic in devenv is no longer needed, since the bootstrapped apps behave similarly to the chainlink node in that aspect. As such, all keygen logic has been removed from the build/devenv directory (keys.go and keys_test.go)
* Removed tests/services/verifier_test.go, it wasn't really testing anything that wasn't already being tested by the env spinup process.
* Common bootstrap operations have been added to services/bootstrap.go; in future PRs bootstrapped apps should become more standard to package.

- KMeans sampling only if the number of embeddings is >= 30720 (25% of a default rowgroup size). 
- Decide on `num_clusters`. We will support 3 fixed cases: 
    - From 0 to 2047: 1 cluster
       - Fast path to enter the index (we only pay 1 dummy distance calculation)
       - Fast path for KMeans (we only assign embeddings and choose the first embedding as centroid)
    - From 2048 to 30719 (25% of a default rowgroup size): 120 clusters
       - Tries to mimic a reasonable cluster-to-point ratio of 1:256
    - From 30720 to 122800: 480 clusters
       - Targeting a cluster-to-point ratio of around 1:256
- Fixing `n_probe` to 24 (around 5% of the data if rowgroups are full). 128 was too big for our (future) default scenario of per-rowgroup search. We aim for a range oof 0.80-0.90 recall.
- Supress warning in SuperKMeans when less than 128 clusters are created with HierarchicalSuperKMeans
