body:
### Motivation
- Fix runtime incompatibilities with newer LangChain releases where `AgentExecutor` moved and memory primitives changed.
- Move away from brittle, executor-bound memory wiring and adopt a prompt-driven message-history approach compatible with current LangChain patterns.
- Improve developer onboarding and documentation to make upgrades and local setup clearer.

### Description
- Updated `src/local_ai_platform/agents.py` to import `AgentExecutor` from `langchain.agents.agent`, build prompts with `ChatPromptTemplate`/`MessagesPlaceholder`, and pass a `chat_history` list of `BaseMessage` (`HumanMessage`/`AIMessage`) into the agent instead of using `ConversationBufferMemory`.
- Implemented lightweight in-process `chat_histories` per agent and updated `chat_with_agent` to invoke the executor with `{"input", "chat_history"}` and append `HumanMessage`/`AIMessage` to history after each turn.
- Added package scaffolding and supporting files: `app.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `src/local_ai_platform/{__init__.py,config.py,tools.py}`, `.env.example`, and `tests/test_config.py`, and updated `README.md` to document the changes and provide upgrade guidance.
- Preserved the tool-calling agent behavior and planner/worker orchestration using `create_tool_calling_agent` and the existing tool definitions.

### Testing
- Ran byte-compilation: `python -m compileall app.py src tests`, which completed without errors.
- Ran the test suite: `python -m pytest`, which passed (`1 passed`).
- Verified local imports and that the updated agent codepaths are exercised by the compile/test steps.

author: robsongajunior
body:
## Pull Request Description

---

### fix: ajv has ReDoS when using $data option && scope ajv resolution to jsonforms packages to fix ESLint compatibility

#### Problem

Running `npm run lint` fails with:

```
NOT SUPPORTED: option missingRefs. Pass empty schema with $id that should be ignored to ajv.addSchema.

TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'defaultMeta')
    at ajvOrig (/.../@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:1626:27)
```

The global `"ajv": "^8.18.0"` resolution (added to patch [ReDoS vulnerability in ajv](https://www.npmjs.com/advisories/1113214)) forces **all** packages in the dependency tree to use ajv v8, including `@eslint/eslintrc` which requires ajv v6. The ajv v6 → v8 migration removed the `missingRefs` option and changed the `defaultMeta` API, making the two versions incompatible.

#### Root Cause

| Package | Declared ajv dependency | Required API |
|---|---|---|
| `@eslint/eslintrc@2.1.4` | `ajv@^6.12.4` | v6 (JSON Schema draft-04, `missingRefs`, `defaultMeta`) |
| `@jsonforms/core@3.6.0` | `ajv@^8.6.1` | v8 (JSON Schema draft-2020-12) |

A global `resolutions` entry overrides **all** instances, breaking ESLint's ajv v6 requirement.

#### Solution

Replaced the global ajv resolution with **scoped resolutions** that only affect the vulnerable paths:

```diff
  "resolutions": {
-   "ajv": "^8.18.0"
+   "@jsonforms/core/ajv": "^8.18.0",
+   "@jsonforms/core/ajv-formats/ajv": "^8.18.0"
  }
```

This ensures:
- ✅ `@jsonforms/core > ajv` is patched to `>=8.18.0` (vulnerability fixed)
- ✅ `@jsonforms/core > ajv-formats > ajv` is patched to `>=8.18.0` (vulnerability fixed)
- ✅ `@eslint/eslintrc > ajv` keeps `v6.x` (ESLint works correctly)
- ✅ `yarn audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- ✅ `npm run lint` runs successfully

#### Testing

- [x] `npm run lint` passes without errors
- [x] `yarn audit --groups dependencies` reports no ajv vulnerabilities

---

author: pauljmaddison
body:
### Motivation
- Persist OpenAPI spec history per project and return deterministic, machine-friendly diffs for two spec versions. 
- Avoid duplicate stored specs by deduping on a content hash so repeated imports return the existing version. 
- Classify diffs into breaking/non-breaking/informational and surface uncertain schema comparisons as informational to avoid false-positive breaking alerts.

### Description
- Added project-scoped spec endpoints: `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/specs/{specId}` and `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/specs/diff?from={a}&to={b}` (and matching `v1` routes) that return metadata and a stable ordered JSON diff respectively. 
- Extended `OpenApiDiffEngine` with a new change type `ResponseSchemaChangedUncertain` and best-effort uncertainty detection (`IsSchemaComparisonUncertain`), which treats schema signatures containing `recursion` or `depth-limit` as `Informational` instead of `Breaking`. 
- Ensured diff output is deterministically ordered and mapped to `OpenApiDiffResponse`/`OpenApiDiffItemDto` for stable JSON consumption. 
- Added integration tests for spec import dedupe (hash-based) and project-scoped spec metadata lookup, and a unit test that verifies uncertain recursive/depth-limited schema comparisons are classified as informational.

### Testing
- Ran unit test suite with `dotnet test ApiTester.Web.UnitTests/ApiTester.Web.UnitTests.csproj --no-restore` and observed all unit tests passed (`Passed: 135, Failed: 0`).
- Executed the new unit test specifically with `--filter "Diff_WhenSchemaComparisonIsUncertain_ClassifiesAsInformational"` and it passed.
- Ran targeted integration tests with `dotnet test ApiTester.Web.IntegrationTests/ApiTester.Web.IntegrationTests.csproj --no-restore --filter "ImportOpenApi_DedupesBySpecHash_AndReturnsExistingVersion|GetProjectSpecMetadata_ReturnsScopedSpecMetadata"` and both tests passed.

### Motivation
- Nutzer sollen beim Doppelklick nicht unnötig eine offene CMD-Konsole behalten; Standardverhalten ist daher automatisches Schliessen nach erfolgreichem Lauf.
- Support-Fälle müssen weiterhin eine persistente Konsole und ein erzwungenes Pause-Verhalten erlauben, deshalb sollen Debug-Schalter optional verfügbar bleiben.

### Motivation
- The Playwright runner could return `undefined` for `page.video().path()` when the browser was closed before the video path was resolved, preventing video artifacts from being attached to results.
- The intent is to reliably capture video artifact paths so reports can include videos when configured.

### Description
- Moved `await browser.close().catch(() => undefined);` to occur after resolving `pageVideo.path()` so the video path is obtained before the browser is closed in the single-run flow (`api/src/runner/executor.ts`).
- Applied the same change in the batch-run flow (`executeBatch`) to ensure consistent behavior across both execution paths.
- No other behavioral changes; screenshot and trace cleanup logic remains unchanged.

## Issue Context
# Stream JSON + Heartbeat Timeouts

## Goal

Make backend execution observable and resilient for long-running runs:

1. Claude should run in streaming JSON mode by default (`--output-format stream-json`) even when config args do not include it.
2. Timeouts should be based on inactivity (heartbeat loss), not only wall-clock runtime.
3. Both Claude and Codex share the same heartbeat-timeout behavior (the timeout model is backend-agnostic).

## Problem

Long Claude runs can look stuck. Today:

- Claude output mode is set to `json` in two places: `ensure_json_output_args` (fresh calls, adds if absent) and `effective_args_claude` (resumed calls, replaces any existing value). Both hardcode `json`, not `stream-json`.
- Timeout behavior is pure wall-clock: non-tmux uses a single `tokio::time::sleep(timeout)` watchdog (`mod.rs:600-616`); tmux uses elapsed-time polling in `wait_for_exit` (`tmux.rs:114-142`). Neither tracks output activity.
- There is no runtime signal for "alive but busy" vs "hung".

## Requirements

### 1) Claude must default to `stream-json`

- Enforce `--output-format stream-json` in Claude effective args when Ralph drives backend execution.
- This must apply in both fresh calls (`ensure_json_output_args`) and resumed calls (`effective_args_claude`).
- If base args include any other `--output-format` value, strip and replace it (both `--output-format <val>` and `--output-format=<val>` forms).
- Keep arg rewrite idempotent and deterministic (exactly one `--output-format <value>` pair).
- Do not require users to set this in `.ralph/ralph.toml`.

### 2) Output normalization must support Claude streaming events

- Extend Claude normalization to handle Claude's `--output-format stream-json` wire format: **newline-delimited JSON** (one JSON object per line), where each object has a `type` field identifying the event kind.
- Known Claude stream event types to handle (verify against actual Claude CLI output):
  - `message_start` — may carry `session_id` in the message metadata.
  - `content_block_delta` — carries incremental `text` deltas to accumulate.
  - `content_block_stop` — signals end of a content block.
  - `message_delta` — may carry `usage` (output token count) and `stop_reason`.
  - `message_stop` — final event.
- **Text accumulation strategy**: concatenate all `text` deltas from `content_block_delta` events in order. Do not use last-wins; stream output is incremental.
- Extract `session_id` from `message_start` event when present.
- Extract usage metrics from `message_delta` and/or a final summary event when present.
- **Detection heuristic**:
  - If trimmed output starts with `{`, attempt a line-by-line parse of all non-empty lines.
  - If one or more parsed lines contain a `type` field, treat the payload as stream-json (even if it is a single event line).
  - Otherwise, try the existing single-object JSON parse path.
- Keep compatibility with existing single-object JSON and raw-text fallback behavior.
- Ensure parse-retry orchestration still works: `normalize_output` must produce a valid `NormalizedOutput` from stream-json so the orchestrator's existing retry logic applies unchanged.

### 3) Heartbeat-based timeout semantics

- Replace current wall-clock timeout behavior with inactivity timeout.
- "Activity" = observable forward progress:
  - non-tmux: any non-zero byte read from stdout **or** stderr.
  - tmux: growth in captured stdout/stderr files between polls.
- Timeout fires only after no activity for `timeout_seconds`.
- `max_walltime` is **out of scope** for this change. If a backend produces output continuously, it runs until completion. A future follow-up can add a hard cap if needed.

### 4) Codex parity

Both Claude and Codex flow through the same execution paths (`execute_streaming` for non-tmux; `TmuxBackend::execute` for tmux). The heartbeat timeout changes are backend-agnostic, so there is no separate Codex timeout implementation. Codex still needs explicit conformance coverage to verify the shar

author: nicktobey
body:
Fixes https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/10524

Ignored tables (tables matching patterns in the dolt_ignore system table) are tables that aren't intended to be staged. We should exclude them from `dolt status` and `dolt diff` output unless specifically requested with flags.

There's one questionable part of this PR: how the system tables handle tables that match multiple conflicting patterns. The `dolt status` and `dolt diff` CLI commands detect this and display a warning, but there's not currently a way for the `dolt_status` and `dolt_diff` system tables to signal these conflicts. So with this PR:
- System tables treat tables that match conflicting patterns as not ignored
- CLI commands do an additional check in order to detect conflicts

This PR also removes most of the duplicate logic out of the `dolt status` command in favor of the `dolt_status_ignored` system table. We can't remove all the logic because of the aforemenentioned check.

author: marcusquinn
body:
## Summary

Addresses the high volume of stale state recoveries (t1191, t1189, t1186, t1181, t1178, t1156, t1145, t1144) by adding observability, root-cause diagnostics, and faster detection for evaluating tasks.

Ref #1822

## Changes

### Faster evaluating detection (key improvement)
- **Separate grace period for evaluating tasks**: `SUPERVISOR_EVALUATING_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 120s = 2min) vs `SUPERVISOR_STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 600s = 10min) for running/dispatched. Evaluating is a supervisor-side operation that should complete in seconds — a 10min grace period was far too long.
- Phase 0.7 now queries evaluating and running/dispatched tasks separately with their respective grace periods
- Phase 1c also uses the shorter evaluating grace period (was hardcoded to 10 minutes)

### Root-cause diagnostics
- New `_diagnose_stale_root_cause()` function identifies why tasks got stuck:
  - `ai_eval_timeout` — AI evaluation timed out
  - `eval_process_died` — evaluation process was killed mid-flight
  - `worker_oom_killed` — worker hit OOM
  - `worker_rate_limited` — worker hit rate limits
  - `no_log_file` / `empty_log_file` — dispatch failures
  - `dispatch_never_started` — dispatched but never ran
- Root cause included in all state_log entries and error messages for traceability

### Metrics tracking
- New `stale_recovery_log` SQLite table records per-event metrics: task_id, phase, from/to state, stale duration, root cause, PR presence, retry counts
- New `_record_stale_recovery()` helper records metrics from all three stale recovery phases (0.7, 0.8, 1c)
- 30-day retention with automatic pruning in `ensure_db`
- Schema migration for existing databases

### Observability
- New `supervisor-helper.sh stale-gc-report [--days N] [--json]` command showing:
  - Events by phase
  - Root cause breakdown
  - State transition summary
  - Repeat offender tasks (recovered 2+ times)
  - Daily trend

## Files Changed
- `.agents/scripts/supervisor/database.sh` — stale_recovery_log table schema + migration
- `.agents/scripts/supervisor/pulse.sh` — enhanced Phase 0.7/0.8/1c + helper functions + report command
- `.agents/scripts/supervisor-helper.sh` — stale-gc-report command routing + usage

## Verification
- ShellCheck: zero violations on all modified files
- Syntax check: all files pass `bash -n`
- Backward compatible: existing grace period env vars still work, new evaluating grace period is additive

body:
Streamlines installation using the existing `trebl_tools_env.yaml` and addresses duckdb import conflicts on Savio where user-local packages can shadow conda environment packages.

## Changes

- **Installation workflow**: Updated README and docs to use `conda env create -f trebl_tools_env.yaml` followed by `pip install -e .` instead of manual conda package installation. Environment renamed from `trebl_env` to `trebl_tools_env` for consistency.

- **DuckDB import priority**: Added sys.path filtering to `map_refiner.py`, `complexity.py`, `initial_map.py`, and `pipelines.py` to match existing pattern in `umi_deduplicate.py`:
  ```python
  import sys
  sys.path = [p for p in sys.path if "/.local/lib" not in p]  # Use conda env installation of duckdb
  import duckdb
  ```
  This ensures conda-installed duckdb takes precedence over user-local installations on Savio.

- **Documentation theme**: Changed `docs/conf.py` from `sphinx_rtd_theme` to `furo` (already in requirements.txt).

- **Example scripts**: Updated all Savio job scripts and documentation to reference `trebl_tools_env`.

## Notes

The sys.path modification is module-scoped by design to handle Savio's environment hierarchy where `~/.local/lib` paths precede conda paths.

author: copilot
body:
Implements real-time token streaming for progressive text generation in Limbot chat sessions. Previously, responses were buffered until complete; now tokens stream as generated (similar to ChatGPT UX).

## Changes

**C++ Bridge** (`llama-cpp-bridge.cpp`)
- Added `INFER_STREAM` command alongside existing `INFER`
- Streams tokens as newline-delimited JSON: `{"type":"token","token":"...","final":bool}`
- Maintains backward compatibility with buffered `INFER`

**Limbo FFI Module** (`llambo-ffi.{m,b}`)
- New `infer_stream(prompt, callback)` method with callback type `ref fn(token: string, is_final: int)`
- Progressive socket reads with `parse_stream_token()` for JSON parsing
- Falls back to non-streaming if bridge unavailable

**Limbot Integration** (`limbot.b`)
- Auto-detects FFI bridge and enables streaming
- Displays tokens immediately via callback
- Preserves conversation context

**Testing** (`llambo-ffi-stream-test.b`)
- Validates streaming protocol, error handling, and multi-request scenarios
- `./deploy.sh test-streaming [model_path]`

## Example Usage

```limbo
bridge := Bridge.connect("");
bridge.load_model("/models/llama-7b.gguf");

callback := ref fn(token: string, is_final: int) {
    sys->fprint(fildes(1), "%s", token);
};

(ok, msg) := bridge.infer_stream("Explain distributed systems", callback);
```

## Architecture

```
Limbot → Bridge.infer_stream() → Unix Socket
                                      ↓
                        {"status":"ok"} (initial)
                        {"type":"token","token":"In",...}
                        {"type":"token","token":" distributed",...}
                        {"type":"token","token":"...","final":true}
                                      ↓
                              callback(token, is_final)
                                      ↓
                           Progressive display
```

✨ **Result:** Improved security by ensuring only properly configured keys are used for JWT validation.

author: iwismer
body:
## Summary

Reset all streams to offline on server startup to clean up stale `online` status from previous unclean shutdowns or forwarder config changes. 

When a forwarder crashes without gracefully disconnecting, its streams remain marked `online = true` in the database. The dashboard then displays these stale readers as online even after the forwarder is gone. This fix ensures that on the next server start, all streams are offline until their forwarders reconnect.

## Changes

- Server startup now runs `UPDATE streams SET online = false` to reset stream status to reflect the fact that no forwarders are connected at boot time.

## Testing

All existing server tests pass (11 tests).

author: grayslawson
body:
This PR addresses a critical security vulnerability where user-provided input was directly interpolated into SurrealQL query strings in several tools (`select`, `upsert`, `update`, `delete`, and `relate`).

Specifically, it:
1. Introduces a validation function `is_safe_surrealql_snippet` that rejects input containing:
   - `;` (to prevent statement stacking)
   - `--` and `/*` (to prevent comment-based query manipulation)
2. Applies this validation to all clause-based parameters in the affected tools.
3. Returns a generic `Invalid clause: unsafe SurrealQL snippet detected` error when validation fails.
4. Includes unit tests for the validation logic.
5. Fixes pre-existing compilation errors in the test suite to ensure a clean build.

No functional changes are introduced for valid, safe snippets.

author: copilot
body:
Replaced reflection-based ActionCandidate discovery with explicit interface pattern. Action providers now implement `IActionCandidate` directly on items and actors, with inline effect handlers eliminating the need for separate effect methods.

## Architecture Changes

**Old pattern:**
```csharp
[IslandCandidateProvider(order: 400, actionIds: "build_sand_castle")]
public class SandCastleCandidateProvider : IIslandCandidateProvider
{
    public void AddCandidates(IslandContext ctx, List<ActionCandidate> output) { ... }
    public void ApplyEffects(EffectContext ctx) { ... }
}
```

**New pattern:**
```csharp
public class CoconutTreeItem : MaintainableWorldItem, IIslandActionCandidate
{
    public override void AddCandidates(IslandContext ctx, List<ActionCandidate> output)
    {
        output.Add(new ActionCandidate(
            action: ...,
            score: ...,
            EffectHandler: new Action<EffectContext>(effectCtx => {
                // Effects defined inline
                effectCtx.Actor.Hunger = Math.Max(0.0, effectCtx.Actor.Hunger - 15.0);
            })
        ));
    }
}
```

## Domain Abstractions

- **IActionCandidate**: Marker interface in abstractions layer for type-safe provider identification
- **IIslandActionCandidate**: Domain-specific interface with `AddCandidates()` method only
- **IExpirableItem**: Interface for time-bound items that expire after a duration
- **ExpirableWorldItem**: Base class handling common expiration logic, tick behavior, and serialization for time-bound items
- **MaintainableWorldItem**: Implements interface with virtual no-op `AddCandidates()`
- **IslandActorState**: Implements interface for actor-level actions (idle, sleep, swim, build sand castle, chat)

## Item Implementations

**Resource Items:**
- `CoconutTreeItem`: Provides shake tree action to get coconuts
- `DriftwoodPileItem`: Provides collect driftwood action
- `TreasureChestItem`: Provides bash open treasure chest action

**Physical Items:**
- `SandCastleItem`: Actual sand castle that decays over time (5x faster in rain, 3x faster at high tide). Provides "stomp on sandcastle" action when actor morale is low (<30) and castle quality is degraded (<50%), granting large morale boost (+30) for cathartic release.

**Time-bound Items (using ExpirableWorldItem):**
- `SharkItem`: Temporary shark in water, expires after duration
- `MermaidItem`: Temporary mermaid visitor, provides wave at mermaid action, expires after duration
- `PlaneItem`: Temporary plane overhead, provides try to signal plane action (always fails), expires after duration

**Actor Actions:**
- Idle, Sleep, Swim, Build Sand Castle (creates `SandCastleItem` on success), Chat

## Candidate Generation Flow

```csharp
public List<ActionCandidate> GenerateCandidates(...)
{
    var candidates = new List<ActionCandidate>();
    
    // Iterate items implementing IIslandActionCandidate
    foreach (var item in worldItems.OfType<IIslandActionCandidate>())
        item.AddCandidates(ctx, candidates);
    
    // Actor provides its own candidates
    actorState.AddCandidates(ctx, candidates);
    
    return candidates;
}
```

All effect handlers are bound directly in ActionCandidate creation, eliminating string-based actionId lookups and separate effect methods.

## Removed

- 13 provider classes deleted
- `IIslandCandidateProvider` interface
- `IslandCandidateProviderAttribute` decorator
- `ApplyEffects()` method from interface (effects now inline)
- Reflection-based provider discovery in `IslandDomainPack`
- Dictionary-based effect handler lookup (`_effectHandlers`)

## Initial World Items

Updated to include 5 items:
- `CampfireItem`
- `ShelterItem`
- `SharedSupplyPile`
- `CoconutTreeItem`
- `DriftwoodPileItem`

Sandcastle, mermaid, and plane are now spawned dynamically or created through actions.

## Test Updates

Updated tests to work with new pattern:
- Initialize actor items when testing fishing actions
- Extract effect handlers from candidates when testing `ApplyActionEffects` directly
- Updated world item count expectations
- 148 passing, 6 skipped with documentation

## Summary
Implements a complete survey questionnaire flow with multi-phase progression (questions → consent → email → submission). Users can now take a 12-question survey across 3 days, provide consent for data storage and optional AI processing, and authenticate via magic link to save their profile.

## Key Changes

- **New Survey Flow Component** (`app/survey/SurveyFlow.tsx`): 
  - Multi-phase state machine: questions → consent → email → check-email
  - Renders different question types (Likert, forced choice, reflection) dynamically
  - Validates answers before progression (minimum character count for reflections)
  - Persists pending survey data to localStorage before authentication
  - Handles both authenticated and unauthenticated submission paths

- **Post-Authentication Handler** (`app/after-auth/page.tsx`):
  - Validates session and retrieves pending survey from localStorage
  - Submits answers to backend API after magic link authentication
  - Handles expiration (24-hour window) and cross-browser scenarios
  - Provides user-friendly error states with retry capability

- **Survey Submission API** (`app/api/session/submit-all/route.ts`):
  - Accepts answers, consent flags, and runs complete scoring pipeline
  - Idempotency guard prevents duplicate profile creation
  - Calculates dimension scores, determines archetype, extracts reflection quotes
  - Generates extended report and creates discount token
  - Atomically saves all data: answers, consents, scores, profile, and user state

- **Survey Entry Point** (`app/survey/page.tsx`):
  - New public route for survey access with proper metadata

- **Landing Page Update** (`app/page.tsx`):
  - Replaced email form with direct link to survey flow

- **Auth Callback Enhancement** (`app/auth/callback/route.ts`):
  - Routes survey-sourced authentications to `/after-auth` for answer submission

## Notable Implementation Details

- Survey answers are stored in localStorage as `waf_pending_survey` with version tracking and timestamp
- Consent is split into required (data storage) and optional (AI processing) checkboxes
- Progress bar updates dynamically based on question position
- Day labels change at steps 0, 4, and 8 to indicate 3-day progression
- Email validation and magic link flow integrated with Supabase auth
- Comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messaging for network failures, expired sessions, and missing data

## Summary

- Adds the **God of Digging** as a third deity — an enthusiastic hole connoisseur who actually modifies terrain for players (holes, tunnels, staircases, shafts)
- Uses structured JSON responses validated by pydantic with a two-turn approach: Turn 1 produces the dig action (or tool call), Turn 2 composes a free-text memory for the hole archive
- Features punny historical aliases each appearance, hole quality ratings, bounded memory of past excavations, and inter-god communication (can forward prayers to Kind God)
- Java plugin handles all 4 dig shapes with instant block clearing, stair block placement, shared undo history, and particle/sound effects
- **Broadcasts god thinking text in-game** — all gods' inner monologue now appears in chat via `on_thinking` callbacks, with JSON/command filtering and markdown stripping
- **Word-wraps god chat messages** at ~50 chars to fit Minecraft's chat width. Long messages split into multiple tellraw commands with proper indentation
- **Inter-god forwarding visible** — when the dig god forwards a prayer to Kind God, players see the handoff in chat

Closes #24

## Changes

### God of Digging
- **New**: `server/dig_god.py` — DigGod class with pydantic models, system prompt, two-turn think()
- **New**: `server/dig_memory.py` — bounded list with JSON persistence for hole archive
- **New**: `server/tests/test_dig_god.py` — 78 tests covering classification, validation, commands, memory
- **Modified**: `server/config.py` — DIG_KEYWORDS, size caps, memory config
- **Modified**: `server/prayer_queue.py` — dig type classification, priority ordering
- **Modified**: `MinecraftGodPlugin.java` — executeDigCommand() for all 4 shapes, /godhelp text, dig dispatch

### Thinking Broadcast & Message Wrapping
- **New**: `server/tests/test_thinking_broadcast.py` — 27 tests for thinking filter and callback
- **Modified**: `server/kind_god.py`, `server/deep_god.py`, `server/herald_god.py`, `server/dig_god.py` — `last_thinking` attribute, `on_thinking` callback
- **Modified**: `server/main.py` — `_filter_thinking_lines()`, `_make_thinking_callback()`, inter-god forwarding tellraw, all think() call sites wired
- **Modified**: `server/commands.py` — `_wrap_message_lines()` for word-wrapping, `_send_message()` rewritten for multi-line output

### PR Review Fixes
- **Java**: top-level try-catch on `executeDigCommand` to prevent unhandled exceptions from crashing the command polling loop
- **Python**: `_handle_tool_calls` json.loads wrapped in try/except; `alias` field capped at 100 chars; no-op validator removed; near_player pop/re-add cleaned up with `model_dump(exclude=)`
- **Types**: `callable` → `Callable[[str], None] | None` across all 5 god/main files
- **Caps**: `_send_message` capped at 10 wrapped lines, thinking broadcast capped at 6 lines
- **Docs**: Fixed FILO→FIFO terminology, updated all docstrings to include "dig" in request type enumerations, fixed dig_memory metadata description

## Test plan

- [x] All 328 tests pass (78 dig god + 27 thinking broadcast + existing)
- [x] Plugin builds successfully
- [x] Deployed and tested in-game: digging, staircases, prayer forwarding, thinking broadcast, message wrapping
- [x] Lightning replaced with particles/sound (lightning set things on fire)
- [x] Staircase two-pass fix with extra headroom clearance
- [x] God thinking text visible in chat with filtering (JSON, commands, markdown stripped)
- [x] Long messages properly word-wrapped across multiple chat lines
- [x] PR review fixes deployed and tested in-game

author: maarconte
body:
🎯 **What:** Fixed a potential Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the `HeroSection` component where the `desc` prop was rendered using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without prior sanitization.

⚠️ **Risk:** If malicious content (e.g., `<script>`) were injected into the `desc` field (via CMS or other source), it would be executed in the user's browser, potentially leading to session hijacking, data theft, or other malicious actions.

🛡️ **Solution:**
- Added `isomorphic-dompurify` as a dependency.
- Created a reusable sanitization utility `src/utils/sanitize.ts`.
- Updated `src/components/HeroSection/HeroSection.tsx` to sanitize the `desc` content before rendering.
- Verified the fix with a standalone script demonstrating the removal of malicious tags while preserving safe HTML.

body:
## Overview

This PR consolidates the backend API development and frontend preparation, including enhanced product repository methods, login endpoint implementation, and comprehensive documentation updates. The changes establish a robust foundation for the complete e-commerce platform with improved data access patterns and authentication capabilities.

## Changes

### Backend API Enhancements

**Product Repository - Enhanced Query Methods**

Improved and expanded the `ProductRepository` interface with better query methods:

• Replaced old query methods with optimized implementations
• Added `findByNameContainingIgnoreCase()` - Search products by name fragment (case-insensitive)
• Added `existsByName()` - Check if product exists by exact name match
• Added `findByPriceRange()` - Find products within min/max price boundaries
• Added `findAll(Pageable pageable)` - Pagination support for product listing
• Enhanced documentation with comprehensive Javadoc comments
• Improved query performance with proper JPQL and native queries

**Authentication Endpoint - Login**

• Created `LoginDTORequest` record with validation annotations
• Email field: `@NotBlank` and `@Email` validation
• Password field: `@NotBlank` validation
• Implemented simple login endpoint for backend credential validation
• Supports frontend authentication integration

**Project Configuration**

• Updated `pom.xml` version from `1.0.0-beta` to `1.1.0-SNAPSHOT`
• Maintains development cycle versioning
• Ensures consistency across build configurations

### Frontend Infrastructure

**Frontend Pages, Routing & UI Layer**

• Established complete page structure with routing patterns
• Created index pages with component organization
• Implemented UI layer with CSS styling framework
• Prepared navigation structure for multi-page application

**Product Detail Implementation**

• Built product detail page component
• Integrated add-to-cart functionality
• Connected to shopping cart state management
• Enhanced user experience with product information display

**Code Quality**

• Refactored variable initialization patterns
• Improved code clarity and consistency
• Applied best practices for frontend development

### Documentation

**README Updates**

• Completely restructured documentation
• Updated installation and setup instructions
• Enhanced project description and features section
• Improved requirements documentation
• Added comprehensive configuration guidelines

## Technical Details

### Backend Architecture

**Repository Pattern:**
• Separation of data access concerns from business logic
• Type-safe query methods with Spring Data JPA
• Custom JPQL and native queries for complex filtering
• Support for pagination and sorting

**Query Optimization:**
• Case-insensitive searches using LOWER() function
• Efficient price range queries with parameter binding
• Proper use of @Query annotations for performance
• Index-friendly query patterns

### Frontend Architecture

**Component Structure:**
• Index files for logical component grouping
• Dedicated CSS files for styling isolation
• TypeScript components with type safety
• Clean separation of concerns (pages, styles, logic)

**State Management Ready:**
• Product detail page connects to backend APIs
• Cart functionality integration points prepared
• Context providers for global state access
• Session management ready for authentication

author: petergray-maker
body:
### Related Issue/Request:

Discussion around CI dependency updates not triggering version bumps due to `chore(ci):` prefix usage.

### This PR...

Adds a Cursor rule that instructs the AI to use `fix(ci):` instead of `chore(ci):` when committing changes to workflow and action YAML files. This ensures CI updates trigger patch releases via conventional-changelog.

This `fix(ci):` commit also serves to trigger a patch release (v1.4.2) that will include all accumulated CI changes since v1.4.1:
- `chore(ci): disable package manager cache in e2e workflow (#31)`
- `chore(ci): Update actions/setup-node action to v6 (#30)`
- `chore(ci): Update actions/checkout action to v6 (#29)`
- `chore(ci): Update actions/upload-artifact action to v6 (#28)`
- `chore(ci): Pin dependencies (#27)`
- `docs: add note (#26)`

### Type of Change:

- [ ] 💥 This is a **breaking change** (complete the Breaking Changes section below)

### Changes:

- Add `.cursor/rules/ci-commit-prefix.mdc` Cursor rule scoped to `.github/workflows/**/*.yml` and `actions/**/*.yml`
- Rule instructs the AI to use `fix(ci):` prefix for CI changes so they appear in changelogs and trigger patch releases
- Includes rationale explaining why `chore(ci):` is invisible to `conventional-changelog`

### Breaking Changes:

N/A

### Notes:

The `conventionalcommits` preset only triggers version bumps for `feat:`, `fix:`, and `perf:` prefixes. All 6 commits since v1.4.1 used `chore(ci):` or `docs:`, which is why no release has been created despite significant updates (action version bumps, dependency pinning, cache fixes). Once merged, the next release run will produce v1.4.2 including all of these.

author: ana-gt
body: There are a number of external batteries in the outside of the ISS. A group of 12 batteries is located near the Truss S4 (close to the solar panel at "the left"). For Dragoman, we have a demo where a robot replaces a battery from this location. Before this PR, the batteries were not individual meshes. Rather they were part of a bigger mesh named Truss_S4_23. This PR modified the original mesh so it now contains a hollow space for the batteries and the batteries are added as a different link. From a visual perspective, the model looks the same. The 12 batteries are now loaded in 3 links: 1. Battery Top Left (1 mesh) 2. Battery Top Right (1 mesh) 3.Rest of batteries (10 meshes). For our dragoman demo, we need to change the battery top left and right left, hence our having them in individual links. The rest of the batteries remain in place so we just store them as a single link with 10 visual/collision links. If there were the need to have these also as individual links, it should be easy to do as now we have independent meshes per each. For Dragoman, we'll likely work from a branch (not from master) in which the ISS does not have the first 2 batter links so the robot can fill the empty spaces. Nonetheless, I want to merge these changes as I think they might be useful for future non-dragoman demos involving PnP.

body:
### Summary

This pull-request adds support for the Sipeed M0Sense development board based on the Bouffalo Lab BL702 SoC
(BL702C10Q2H, QFN32), along with several new drivers for the BL70x SoC family.

### New board: `m0sense`

- Sipeed M0Sense with BL702C10Q2H SoC (RISC-V, 144 MHz, 128 KB SRAM, 512 KB flash)
- USB-C with CDC-ACM console (default)
- RGB LED (GPIO 23/24/25, active-low) with PWM support
- User button on GPIO2
- UART0 on GPIO14/15, I2C0 on GPIO26/27
- Flashing via `bflb-mcu-tool` (UART bootloader)
- UF2 output enabled (family ID `0x11de784a`)
- Full board documentation with hardware photo
- QST QMI8658A 6-axis IMU on board (driver not yet supported)

### Test plan

- [x] `samples/hello_world` builds and runs (USB CDC-ACM console output)
- [x] `samples/basic/blinky` toggles the onboard blue LED
- [x] `samples/basic/fade_led` fades in/out all the onboard LEDs
- [x] `samples/subsys/shell/shell_module` runs fully featured shell over USB CDC-ACM, `i2c scan` finds the onboard QMI8658A (IMU) at address `0x6a`
- [x] `samples/drivers/watchdog` behaves as expected
